# Build: Cursor Repulsion Burst

Up to 1400 particles in one instanced draw call, each circling its own home on its own phase. The pointer opens a hole in the field with a linear falloff inside its radius, and a press fires a shock wave whose front tints the particles it is passing through. The pointer is damped on the CPU before it reaches a uniform, and bursts run in a pool of three slots so overlapping presses produce overlapping waves rather than one wave restarting.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

An orbiting particle field the pointer pushes out of the way, and a press detonates into a shock wave with a heat band.

- Category: cursor
- Runtime cost: webgl
- Dependencies: ogl@^1.0.11

## How it works

1. Three displacements are stacked in field space in the vertex shader before anything becomes a position: an idle orbit, cursor repulsion, then up to three shock waves. Each stage reads the position the previous one produced, so a particle already pushed aside by the cursor is the particle the wave throws.
2. All distances are measured in aspect-corrected space — x multiplied by `uResolution.x / uResolution.y` — and the resulting displacement is divided back out before it is added to the position. Without the correction the repulsion hole is an ellipse on any container that is not square, and the shock ring reaches the side edges before the top.
3. Repulsion is `max(radius - distance, 0) * repel`: linear inside the radius and exactly zero outside it, so the field beyond the pointer is untouched and the whole idea costs one `length()` per particle. A `smoothstep` would be softer but would also mean every particle on screen is permanently displaced a little, which reads as the field sagging toward the cursor.
4. The direction is `v / max(length(v), floor)` rather than `normalize(v)`. A true normalize is undefined at the origin and unstable just outside it, so the particle sitting under the cursor picks a new direction every frame from floating-point noise and buzzes. Dividing by a floor makes the vector shorter than unit length near the centre, so the push fades in and the direction stays put.
5. A burst slot is `vec4(originX, originY, progress, active)`. The displacement is `(0.25 + seed * 0.75) * push * easeOutCubic(t) * settle(t) * reach(d)`, where `settle` walks the whole thing back to zero by t = 1 so the slot can be freed without the field snapping home, and `reach` limits the throw to the neighbourhood of the origin so the burst is not a camera jolt.
6. The heat band is `exp(-b * b)` where `b = (distance - burstRadius * ease) / band`. The shock radius expands on the same cubic ease as the displacement, so only the particles the front is passing through right now take the tint. A flat tint over the whole burst just recolours the field; a Gaussian band travelling through it reads as heat.
7. Only `active` and `progress` change per frame per slot, so a burst costs three vec4 uniforms and a three-iteration loop — no per-particle CPU state and no buffer upload.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `smoothing = 0.0008`
  Fraction of the pointer gap still remaining after one second: a tight ~90ms tail, because a repulsion hole that lags is read as broken rather than as smooth — the hole has a visible edge, unlike a glow. Raise it past ~0.01 and the field is still opening where the cursor was half a second ago.
- `cursorRadius = 0.22`
  Field units, where 1 is the container HEIGHT. Roughly a fifth of the panel, so the hole is obviously deliberate but the field still dominates. Past ~0.45 the pointer clears most of the visible particles and there is nothing left to displace.
- `repel = 0.85`
  Displacement at the centre of the field, as a fraction of the radius. Below ~0.4 the hole never actually opens — particles crowd instead of clearing. Above 1.0 the inner particles are pushed past the rim and pile into a bright ring, which is the same artefact as a hard-edged mask.
- `BURST_SLOTS = 3`
  Concurrent waves. One slot means a second press restarts the wave from zero, which visibly sucks the first one back into its origin. Three covers a fast double or triple click, and each slot is a vec4 and a loop iteration, so the ceiling is set by taste rather than by cost.
- `burstDuration = 1.1`
  Seconds of life. Under ~0.6 the wave is gone before the eye finds it; over ~2 the field spends most of its time recovering and a second press lands in a field that is still deformed.
- `burstRadius / BURST_BAND = 0.55 / 0.085`
  How far the front travels, and how thick it is. The band is roughly 15% of the travel, which is a front rather than a wash — take it past ~0.25 and the Gaussian covers the whole burst at once, which is indistinguishable from tinting every particle.
- `burstPush = 0.17`
  Peak displacement in field units, multiplied by a per-particle 0.25-1.0. The spread is what gives the wave a ragged front; a uniform magnitude produces a clean expanding circle, which reads as a UI ripple rather than as a detonation.
- `MAX_DPR = 1.5`
  Additive fill is the entire cost here and it scales with the square of the ratio. These are soft round dots with no fine detail, so a third sample per axis resolves nothing a viewer can see and costs 78% more fragments.

## API

```ts
function CursorRepulsionBurst(props: { density?: number; maxCount?: number; sizeRange?: readonly [number, number]; cursorRadius?: number; repel?: number; burstPush?: number; burstRadius?: number; burstDuration?: number; smoothing?: number; breathe?: number; opacity?: number; colorA?: string; colorB?: string; heatColor?: string; background?: string; seed?: number | string; className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `density: number` — default `1100`
  Particles per megapixel of container area.
- `maxCount: number` — default `1400`
  Population ceiling, and the size the buffers are allocated at.
- `sizeRange: readonly [number, number]` — default `[1.6, 5.2]`
  Particle size in CSS pixels, biased toward the small end.
- `cursorRadius: number` — default `0.22`
  Repulsion radius in field units, where 1 is the container height.
- `repel: number` — default `0.85`
  Displacement at the centre of the repulsion field, as a fraction of its radius.
- `burstPush: number` — default `0.17`
  Peak burst displacement in field units, before the per-particle spread.
- `burstRadius: number` — default `0.55`
  How far a shock front travels before it dies.
- `burstDuration: number` — default `1.1`
  Life of one burst in seconds.
- `smoothing: number` — default `0.0008`
  Fraction of the pointer gap still remaining after one second.
- `breathe: number` — default `0.22`
  Depth of the orbit-radius breathing, 0 to 0.5.
- `opacity: number` — default `0.9`
  Overall alpha multiplier.
- `colorA: string` — default `'#8fb6ff'`
  First tint. Any value ogl's Color accepts.
- `colorB: string` — default `'#e6ecf7'`
  Second tint; each particle mixes between the two.
- `heatColor: string` — default `'#ff8a3c'`
  Colour of the shock front.
- `background: string` — default `'#06070b'`
  Opaque clear colour the additive field is composited onto.
- `seed: number | string` — default `'cursor-repulsion-burst'`
  Seeds the scatter, sizes, phases and burst magnitudes.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the root container via `cn`.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
/** Floor on the population. Below this the field reads as a few stray specks. */
const MIN_COUNT = 220;
/** Slots in the burst pool. Three overlapping waves is the most anyone produces. */
const BURST_SLOTS = 3;
/** Width of the Gaussian heat band, in field units. */
const BURST_BAND = 0.085;
/** Fraction of the presence gap left after a second. ~200ms in and out. */
const PRESENCE_SMOOTHING = 0.007;
/** Size distribution exponent. Above 1 crowds the population into small sizes. */
const SIZE_BIAS = 1.8;
/**
 * Fill cost scales with dpr squared and these are soft round dots with no fine
 * detail, so a third sample per axis resolves nothing a viewer can see.
 */
const MAX_DPR = 1.5;
/** Field-space bounds. Wider than 0..1 so orbits never bare the edges. */
const HOME_MIN = -0.06;
const HOME_MAX = 1.06;

/** The reduced-motion still: a frozen frame with the pointer and one wave in it. */
const STILL_ELAPSED = 6.5;
const STILL_CURSOR: readonly [number, number] = [0.34, 0.56];
const STILL_BURST: readonly [number, number, number] = [0.66, 0.42, 0.42];

export function CursorRepulsionBurst({
  density = 1100,
  maxCount = 1400,
  sizeRange = [1.6, 5.2],
  cursorRadius = 0.22,
  repel = 0.85,
  burstPush = 0.17,
  burstRadius = 0.55,
  burstDuration = 1.1,
  smoothing = 0.0008,
  breathe = 0.22,
  opacity = 0.9,
  colorA = '#8fb6ff',
  colorB = '#e6ecf7',
  heatColor = '#ff8a3c',
  background = '#06070b',
  seed = 'cursor-repulsion-burst',
  className,
}: CursorRepulsionBurstProps) {
  const host = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const stage = useRef<Stage | null>(null);
  const [unsupported, setUnsupported] = useState(false);

  const { width, height } = useResizeObserver(host);
  const size = useRef({ width, height });
  size.current = { width, height };

  const reduced = useReducedMotion();
  const visible = useVisibility();
  const { inView } = useInView(host, { rootMargin: '10%' });
  const ready = width > 1 && height > 1;

  const [minSize = 1.6, maxSize = 5.2] = sizeRange;

  /* Raw pointer target in field space, or null until a real move has happened —
     which is not the same as a pointer resting at the bottom-left corner. */
  const target = useRef<{ x: number; y: number } | null>(null);
  const inside = useRef(false);
  /** The damped follower, seeded at the centre so the first move eases outward. */
  const follow = useRef({ x: 0.5, y: 0.5 });
  const presence = useRef(0);

  const slots = useRef<BurstSlot[]>(
    Array.from({ length: BURST_SLOTS }, () => ({ x: 0.5, y: 0.5, t: 0, active: false })),
  );
  const nextSlot = useRef(0);

  /* Live numbers the loop reads. Changing one must not rebuild the renderer:
     Chromium drops the OLDEST WebGL context past roughly 16 per process, so a
     rebuild per prop change can blank an unrelated canvas elsewhere on the page. */
  const live = useRef({
    cursorRadius,
    repel,
    burstPush,
    burstRadius,
    burstDuration,
    smoothing,
    breathe,
    opacity,
  });
  live.current = {
    cursorRadius,
    repel,
    burstPush,
    burstRadius,
    burstDuration,
    smoothing,
    breathe,
    opacity,
  };

  useEffect(() => {
    const el = host.current;
    if (!el || !ready) return;

    if (!hasWebGL()) {
      setUnsupported(true);
      return;
    }

    /* ogl creates its own canvas, and it is appended and removed per effect
       run. Reusing one React-owned canvas breaks under StrictMode: the first
       cleanup force-loses the context, and `getContext` on that same element
       afterwards returns the dead one rather than a fresh context — the panel
       is then permanently blank in development and fine in production. */
    const renderer = new Renderer({
      dpr: pixelRatio(MAX_DPR),
      // Opaque: the pass is additive, and additive onto a transparent canvas
      // would have to brighten the page behind it, which the GPU cannot see.
      alpha: false,
      // Nothing occludes anything, so a depth buffer is memory plus a clear.
      depth: false,
      antialias: false,
      // Fill-bound, not shader-bound. The discrete GPU buys nothing here.
      powerPreference: 'low-power',
    });

    const gl = renderer.gl;
    const canvas = gl.canvas;

    const bg = new Color(background);
    gl.clearColor(bg.r, bg.g, bg.b, 1);

    const quad = new Float32Array([-0.5, -0.5, 0.5, -0.5, 0.5, 0.5, -0.5, 0.5]);
    const index = new Uint16Array([0, 1, 2, 0, 2, 3]);

    const total = Math.max(MIN_COUNT, Math.round(maxCount));
    const homes = new Float32Array(total * 2);
    const params = new Float32Array(total * 4);
    const seeds = new Float32Array(total * 4);

    const rng = createRng(seed);
    const lo = Math.max(0.5, Math.min(minSize, maxSize));
    const hi = Math.max(lo + 0.25, Math.max(minSize, maxSize));

    for (let i = 0; i < total; i += 1) {
      homes[i * 2] = randRange(rng, HOME_MIN, HOME_MAX);
      homes[i * 2 + 1] = randRange(rng, HOME_MIN, HOME_MAX);

      // Biased small: a linear distribution puts a quarter of the population in
      // the largest quarter of the range, and the field reads as gravel.
      const sizeT = Math.pow(rng(), SIZE_BIAS);
      params[i * 4] = lo + (hi - lo) * sizeT;
      params[i * 4 + 1] = randRange(rng, 0.004, 0.03);
      // Signed rate with a floor on the magnitude: a particle orbiting at
      // 0.001 rad/s is a particle that is simply not moving.
      params[i * 4 + 2] = (rng() < 0.5 ? -1 : 1) * randRange(rng, 0.12, 0.46);
      // Bigger particles are dimmer, so total light stays roughly constant.
      params[i * 4 + 3] = 0.34 + 0.5 * (1 - sizeT);

      seeds[i * 4] = rng() * Math.PI * 2;
      // Burst magnitude. Per-particle, so the wave has a ragged front rather
      // than a clean expanding circle — a clean circle reads as a UI ripple.
      seeds[i * 4 + 1] = rng();
      seeds[i * 4 + 2] = randRange(rng, 0.35, 1);
      seeds[i * 4 + 3] = rng();
    }

    const geometry = new Geometry(gl, {
      index: { data: index },
      position: { size: 2, data: quad },
      aHome: { size: 2, data: homes, instanced: 1 },
      aParams: { size: 4, data: params, instanced: 1 },
      aSeed: { size: 4, data: seeds, instanced: 1 },
    });

    const uniforms: Uniforms = {
      uResolution: { value: [1, 1] },
      uPixelRatio: { value: renderer.dpr },
      uElapsed: { value: 0 },
      uCursor: { value: [0.5, 0.5] },
      uCursorPresence: { value: 0 },
      uCursorRadius: { value: cursorRadius },
      uRepel: { value: repel },
      uBreathe: { value: clamp(breathe, 0, 0.5) },
      uBursts: { value: new Array<number>(BURST_SLOTS * 4).fill(0) },
      uBurstRadius: { value: burstRadius },
      uBurstPush: { value: burstPush },
      uBurstBand: { value: BURST_BAND },
      uColorA: { value: new Color(colorA) },
      uColorB: { value: new Color(colorB) },
      uHeatColor: { value: new Color(heatColor) },
      uOpacity: { value: opacity },
    };

    const program = new Program(gl, {
      vertex: CURSOR_REPULSION_BURST_VERT,
      fragment: CURSOR_REPULSION_BURST_FRAG,
      uniforms,
      transparent: true,
      depthTest: false,
      depthWrite: false,
      // ogl culls BACK faces by default and the quad's winding is not
      // guaranteed to face the way the driver expects. A culled particle is
      // not dim — it is absent.
      cullFace: false,
    });
    // Additive, overriding the source-over that `transparent: true` selected.
    // Order independent, so a thousand overlapping instances need no sort,
    // which is what makes one draw call possible at all.
    program.setBlendFunc(gl.ONE, gl.ONE);

    const mesh = new Mesh(gl, { geometry, program });

    el.appendChild(canvas);
    canvas.style.display = 'block';

    /* Listeners on the CANVAS, not the window. A document-level handler
       outlives the renderer it was written for, and the rect it measures is not
       the rect being drawn into — after a scroll the hole sits at an offset
       from the cursor. Passive, because nothing here calls preventDefault and a
       non-passive move handler makes the compositor wait for JS on every event. */
    const toField = (event: PointerEvent) => {
      const rect = canvas.getBoundingClientRect();
      if (rect.width === 0 || rect.height === 0) return null;
      return {
        x: (event.clientX - rect.left) / rect.width,
        // Flipped: field y is up, client y is down.
        y: 1 - (event.clientY - rect.top) / rect.height,
      };
    };

    const onMove = (event: PointerEvent) => {
      const point = toField(event);
      if (!point) return;
      target.current = point;
      inside.current = true;
    };

    const onDown = (event: PointerEvent) => {
      const point = toField(event);
      if (!point) return;
      // A press is also a position: on touch there is no hover, so without this
      // the wave would fire from wherever the pointer last happened to be.
      target.current = point;
      inside.current = true;

      const slot = slots.current[nextSlot.current % BURST_SLOTS];
      if (!slot) return;
      nextSlot.current = (nextSlot.current + 1) % BURST_SLOTS;
      slot.x = point.x;
      slot.y = point.y;
      slot.t = 0;
      slot.active = true;
    };

    const onLeave = () => {
      // Position is left where it is. Tweening it back to the centre drags a
      // visible furrow across the field on the way out.
      inside.current = false;
    };

    canvas.addEventListener('pointermove', onMove, { passive: true });
    canvas.addEventListener('pointerdown', onDown, { passive: true });
    canvas.addEventListener('pointerleave', onLeave, { passive: true });
    canvas.addEventListener('pointercancel', onLeave, { passive: true });

    const resize = (w: number, h: number) => {
      renderer.setSize(w, h);
      // `setSize` writes literal px into the canvas's inline style, which wins
      // over any class. Re-asserting percentages keeps it fluid between
      // resize notifications.
      canvas.style.width = '100%';
      canvas.style.height = '100%';

      uniforms.uResolution.value = [gl.drawingBufferWidth, gl.drawingBufferHeight];
      uniforms.uPixelRatio.value = renderer.dpr;

      // Population from area, not a fixed number: the same density reads right
      // in a 320px card and a 2000px hero. The buffers already hold `total`
      // particles in scattered order, so a prefix of them is still spatially
      // even — no rebuild, no reallocation, no new GPU memory.
      const megapixels = (w * h) / 1_000_000;
      const count = clamp(Math.round(megapixels * density), MIN_COUNT, total);
      geometry.setInstancedCount(count);
    };

    const draw = (elapsed: number) => {
      uniforms.uElapsed.value = elapsed;
      renderer.render({ scene: mesh });
    };

    resize(size.current.width, size.current.height);
    stage.current = { renderer, geometry, program, mesh, uniforms, resize, draw };
    draw(0);

    return () => {
      stage.current = null;
      canvas.removeEventListener('pointermove', onMove);
      canvas.removeEventListener('pointerdown', onDown);
      canvas.removeEventListener('pointerleave', onLeave);
      canvas.removeEventListener('pointercancel', onLeave);
      // ogl has no `dispose()`: `remove()` on the geometry deletes its VAOs and
      // every buffer, `remove()` on the program deletes the shaders and the
      // program, and only then is the context worth handing back. Dropping the
      // context is the part that matters — the browser's per-process budget is
      // about sixteen, and a lost one takes an unrelated canvas with it.
      geometry.remove();
      program.remove();
      loseContext(gl);
      canvas.width = 0;
      canvas.height = 0;
      canvas.remove();
    };
  }, [ready, density, maxCount, minSize, maxSize, seed]);

  // Colours are pushed into the live uniforms rather than being effect deps, so
  // recolouring never costs a context.
  useEffect(() => {
    const s = stage.current;
    if (!s) return;
    s.uniforms.uColorA.value.set(colorA);
    s.uniforms.uColorB.value.set(colorB);
    s.uniforms.uHeatColor.value.set(heatColor);
    const bg = new Color(background);
    s.renderer.gl.clearColor(bg.r, bg.g, bg.b, 1);
  }, [colorA, colorB, heatColor, background]);

  // Resize is its own effect: a reflow costs a `setSize` and an instanced-count
  // change, never a buffer rebuild.
  useEffect(() => {
    stage.current?.resize(width, height);
  }, [width, height]);

  useRaf(
    (dt, elapsed) => {
      const s = stage.current;
      if (!s) return;
      const cfg = live.current;

      const aim = target.current;
      if (aim) {
        follow.current.x = damp(follow.current.x, aim.x, cfg.smoothing, dt);
        follow.current.y = damp(follow.current.y, aim.y, cfg.smoothing, dt);
      }
      presence.current = damp(
        presence.current,
        inside.current && aim !== null ? 1 : 0,
        PRESENCE_SMOOTHING,
        dt,
      );

      // Bursts advance on wall-clock seconds, not on frames, so a wave lasts
      // `burstDuration` on a 30Hz phone and on a 144Hz monitor alike.
      const flat = s.uniforms.uBursts.value;
      const life = Math.max(cfg.burstDuration, 0.05);
      let i = 0;
      for (const slot of slots.current) {
        if (slot.active) {
          slot.t += dt / life;
          if (slot.t >= 1) {
            slot.t = 1;
            slot.active = false;
          }
        }
        flat[i * 4] = slot.x;
        flat[i * 4 + 1] = slot.y;
        flat[i * 4 + 2] = slot.t;
        flat[i * 4 + 3] = slot.active ? 1 : 0;
        i += 1;
      }

      const u = s.uniforms;
      // Mutated in place. Assigning a fresh tuple allocates two arrays a frame
      // and defeats ogl's redundant-uniform cache, which compares by length
      // first and then element by element against the array it kept.
      u.uCursor.value[0] = follow.current.x;
      u.uCursor.value[1] = follow.current.y;
      u.uCursorPresence.value = presence.current;
      u.uCursorRadius.value = cfg.cursorRadius;
      u.uRepel.value = cfg.repel;
      u.uBurstPush.value = cfg.burstPush;
      u.uBurstRadius.value = cfg.burstRadius;
      u.uBreathe.value = clamp(cfg.breathe, 0, 0.5);
      u.uOpacity.value = cfg.opacity;

      s.draw(elapsed);
    },
    ready && inView && visible && !reduced && !unsupported,
  );

  /* Reduced motion is a composed still, not an empty box: one frame with the
     pointer parked off-centre and a single wave frozen part-way out, so the
     panel shows what the effect produces. The listeners stay attached and their
     target is never consumed, so moving or clicking changes nothing. */
  useEffect(() => {
    const s = stage.current;
    if (!s || !reduced || !ready) return;
    const [cx = 0.34, cy = 0.56] = STILL_CURSOR;
    const [bx = 0.66, by = 0.42, bt = 0.42] = STILL_BURST;
    s.uniforms.uCursor.value[0] = cx;
    s.uniforms.uCursor.value[1] = cy;
    s.uniforms.uCursorPresence.value = 1;
    const flat = s.uniforms.uBursts.value;
    flat.fill(0);
    flat[0] = bx;
    flat[1] = by;
    flat[2] = bt;
    flat[3] = 1;
    s.draw(STILL_ELAPSED);
  }, [reduced, ready, width, height]);
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Removes the four pointer listeners from the canvas, nulls the stage ref so an in-flight frame cannot touch a dead renderer, then `geometry.remove()` (deletes the VAOs and every buffer), `program.remove()` (deletes the shaders and the program), `loseContext(gl)`, zeroes the canvas dimensions and removes it from the DOM. ogl has no `dispose()`, and dropping the context is the part that matters — the per-process budget is about sixteen, and exceeding it kills the oldest context, which belongs to somebody else.

**Reduced motion.** The render loop never starts. One frame is drawn with the pointer parked at (0.34, 0.56) at full presence and a single wave frozen 42% of the way out, so the panel is a composed still of the effect rather than a static dot field. The listeners stay attached but their target is never consumed, so moving or pressing changes nothing on screen.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Writing pointer events straight into `uCursor`. The hole lands exactly where the last event was: a high-rate trackpad delivers a staircase, and after a stalled frame it is a jump that shoves the whole field sideways in one step. The listener records a target and the loop damps toward it.
- Damping with a per-frame constant (`x += (t - x) * 0.1`) instead of `damp(..., dt)`. The same code produces a noticeably tighter follow at 120Hz than at 60Hz, so the effect is tuned for whatever machine it was written on.
- Using `normalize()` for the repulsion direction. It is undefined at the origin, so the particle under the cursor jitters between random directions every frame — a visible buzzing speck exactly where the eye is.
- Aspect-correcting the distances but not dividing the displacement back out. Particles are then pushed further horizontally than vertically, and the hole slowly shears the field sideways as the pointer moves.
- Restarting one burst slot on every press. The in-flight wave is yanked back to its origin before the new one starts, which looks like a rendering fault rather than a second click. Three round-robin slots let waves overlap.
- Advancing burst progress per frame instead of by `dt / duration`. The wave is then twice as fast on a 120Hz display and half speed on a throttled tab.
- Deactivating a slot while its displacement is still non-zero. Every particle in it snaps home on one frame. The magnitude is multiplied by a settle term that reaches zero exactly when the slot expires.
- Handing ogl a Float32Array for `uniform vec4 uBursts[3]`. ogl resolves the active uniform name `uBursts[0]`, checks `Array.isArray(value)` to decide it is an array uniform, and a Float32Array fails that test — the uniform is silently skipped with a console warning and every burst is invisible. It must be a plain array.
- Leaving ogl's default BACK-face culling on. The quad winding is not guaranteed to face the way the driver expects, and a culled particle is not dim, it is absent — so the field renders empty on some machines and fine on others.
- Owning the canvas in React while calling `loseContext()` on cleanup. Under `reactStrictMode` the effect runs twice and the second `getContext` on that element hands back the dead context: blank in development, fine in production.
- Rebuilding the renderer when a colour changes. Chromium drops the oldest WebGL context past roughly sixteen per process, so recolouring one field can blank a different canvas on the same page. Colours are written into live uniforms.

## Notes

- `pointerdown` sets the pointer target as well as firing the wave. On touch there is no hover, so without it the burst would originate from wherever the pointer last happened to be — usually the previous tap.
- Blending is additive with an opaque clear colour, so a thousand overlapping instances need no depth sort and the whole field is one draw call. The fragment output is premultiplied because the destination is only ever added to.
- The population is derived from container area rather than fixed, and selected with `setInstancedCount` out of buffers allocated once at `maxCount`. Resizing changes the count without touching a byte of GPU memory.
- The scatter runs on `createRng(seed)`, never `Math.random()`, so the field is identical on every load and a visual regression is a real regression.
- Particles inside the repulsion radius also brighten, which stops the hole reading as a bald patch — the field gets denser and hotter at the rim instead.

## Definition of done

The field drifts on its own with no pointer on the page. Move the pointer in and a clear hole opens around it, tracking with a short even lag that is the same on a 60Hz and a 120Hz display, with the rim slightly brighter than the rest of the field. The particle directly under the cursor does not jitter. Press and a wave throws the nearby particles outward with a ragged front, a warm band travelling through them, and they drift back without snapping. Press three times quickly and you get three overlapping waves, not one wave restarting. Leave the panel and the hole closes where it stands. Resize to a wide container and the hole is still round. With reduced motion the panel is a single composed still.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Dot-Cloud Score Cylinder

A score wrapped around a cylinder and drawn entirely in dots: measure rings, vertical bar dividers, and note clusters that light as a playhead sweeps them. Two cylinders are stacked and turned to different yaws so they never present the same face at once, and both live in one buffer. Nothing uses a depth buffer — every dot is flattened to z = 0 before projection, and solidity comes from alpha and point size falling off with the model-space z.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Two counter-rotating cylinders of dots — rings, bar lines, notes — drawn from one buffer with no depth buffer.

- Category: webgl
- Runtime cost: webgl
- Dependencies: three@^0.185.1

## How it works

1. One `Float32Array` pair is filled in six consecutive passes — both cylinders' measure rings, then both cylinders' dividers, then both cylinders' notes. Buffer order is the draw order, so notes end up on top of everything without a sort and without a second object.
2. Identity travels in `aPointData = vec4(instanceIndex, isNote, pointScale, groupIndex)`, so the two cylinders share a geometry and the vertex shader picks the transform: instance 1 is mirrored with `p.z *= -1.0` and yawed -166°, instance 0 is yawed -90°.
3. Both are then yawed by `uSpin` (degrees, advancing linearly at `spinSpeed` per second) and tilted 8° on X, and instance 0 is pushed up by 0.3 *after* the rotation so the stack separation is a pure screen-space offset that does not tip with the spin.
4. Depth is faked from the transformed z: `depthT = clamp((z + 0.6) / 1.2, 0, 1)` drives alpha from 0.25 to 1.0 and point size from 0.65 to 1.0, so the far wall of the cylinder recedes without a depth test.
5. The playhead is `mod(floor(uElapsed / uNoteInterval), uGroupCount)`, computed in the vertex shader from the clock that is already there. A note group whose index matches gets 2x point size and full alpha, so highlighting a beat costs no React render and no uniform write.
6. Angles within each ring are sorted before being written into the buffer, and `gl_PointSize` gets the same clamp-plus-area-compensated-alpha treatment as every other point field here.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `BASE_SCALE = 1.5`
  Applied in the shader, not baked into the buffer, so re-framing the piece never re-uploads a vertex.
- `TILT = 8.0 degrees`
  X tilt. Below ~4° the cylinder collapses to a straight band and stops reading as a cylinder; past ~15° you look down the tube and the far wall crowds the near one.
- `INSTANCE_B_YAW = -166.0 degrees`
  Not -180. At exactly half a turn the two cylinders present mirror-image faces and the pair looks like one object reflected; 166° keeps them legibly distinct through the whole rotation.
- `STACK_OFFSET = 0.3`
  Vertical separation, applied after `rotateX` so it is screen-space. Applied before, the offset would tilt with the cylinder and the two would drift into each other as they turn.
- `DEPTH_HALF_RANGE = 0.6`
  z is normalised over ±0.6 while the cloud actually spans ±0.75, so the nearest and furthest dots saturate. Normalising over the exact range leaves the middle band looking flat.
- `DEPTH_MIN_SIZE / DEPTH_MAX_SIZE = 0.65 / 1.0`
  Far dots at 65% of near dots. Alpha alone is not enough — without the size falloff the far wall reads as a grey copy of the near one rather than as distance.
- `NOTE_ACTIVE_SCALE = 2.0`
  Point size multiplier for the lit note group. Area goes as the square, so 2x is a 4x brighter mark — visible at a glance without any colour change being required.
- `spinSpeed = 12 degrees/second`
  One revolution every 30s. The original ran at 1°/s, which is right for an ambient full-page object and far too slow to read in a preview card. Linear either way: easing it would make it look like it is arriving somewhere.
- `MEASURE_SCALE / NOTE_SCALE = 0.7 / 1.4`
  Notes are exactly double the measure dots so they survive the depth size falloff on the far wall, where a measure dot is already down to 0.46.

## API

```ts
function CylinderDotScore(props: { ringCount?: number; ringDots?: number; dividerCount?: number; dividerDots?: number; noteGroups?: number; noteDots?: number; spinSpeed?: number; noteInterval?: number; dotScale?: number; viewScale?: number; opacity?: number; color?: string; noteColor?: string; seed?: number | string; className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `ringCount: number` — default `10`
  Measure rings per cylinder, split evenly above and below the equator gap.
- `ringDots: number` — default `260`
  Dots in each measure ring.
- `dividerCount: number` — default `8`
  Vertical bar dividers per cylinder.
- `dividerDots: number` — default `34`
  Dots making up each divider.
- `noteGroups: number` — default `6`
  Note clusters per cylinder; the playhead cycles through them.
- `noteDots: number` — default `26`
  Dots per note cluster.
- `spinSpeed: number` — default `12`
  Degrees of yaw per second. Linear.
- `noteInterval: number` — default `1.2`
  Seconds each note group stays lit.
- `dotScale: number` — default `1`
  Global dot radius multiplier in CSS pixels.
- `viewScale: number` — default `0.62`
  Model-to-pixel scale as a fraction of the container short side.
- `opacity: number` — default `1`
  Multiplier applied to every dot.
- `color: string` — default `'#7d838c'`
  Measure and divider dot colour.
- `noteColor: string` — default `'#ffffff'`
  Note dot colour; lit notes go fully to this.
- `seed: number | string` — default `'cylinder-dot-score'`
  Seeds ring angles and note scatter for a stable, hydration-safe layout.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the host element via `cn`.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function CylinderDotScore({
  ringCount = 10,
  ringDots = 260,
  dividerCount = 8,
  dividerDots = 34,
  noteGroups = 6,
  noteDots = 26,
  spinSpeed = 12,
  noteInterval = 1.2,
  dotScale = 1,
  viewScale = 0.62,
  opacity = 1,
  color = '#7d838c',
  noteColor = '#ffffff',
  seed = 'cylinder-dot-score',
  className,
}: CylinderDotScoreProps) {
  const host = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const stage = useRef<Stage | null>(null);
  const [unsupported, setUnsupported] = useState(false);

  const { width, height } = useResizeObserver(host);
  const size = useRef({ width, height });
  size.current = { width, height };

  const reduced = useReducedMotion();
  const ready = width > 0 && height > 0;

  useEffect(() => {
    const el = host.current;
    if (!el || !ready) return;

    if (!hasWebGL()) {
      setUnsupported(true);
      return;
    }

    const renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer({ antialias: false, alpha: true });
    renderer.setPixelRatio(pixelRatio());
    renderer.setClearAlpha(0);

    const scene = new THREE.Scene();
    const camera = new THREE.OrthographicCamera(-1, 1, 1, -1, 0.1, 10);
    camera.position.z = 1;

    const rng = createRng(seed);

    /* ------------------------------------------------------------------
       Buffer layout IS the draw order. Points are blended in the order they
       appear, with depth testing off, so the six passes below are written
       consecutively into one pair of arrays: both cylinders' measures, then
       both cylinders' dividers, then both cylinders' notes. Notes last means
       notes on top, everywhere, without a sort and without a second object.
       ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
    const perCylinder = ringCount * ringDots + dividerCount * dividerDots + noteGroups * noteDots;
    const total = perCylinder * 2;

    const positions = new Float32Array(total * 3);
    const pointData = new Float32Array(total * 4);
    let cursor = 0;

    const write = (
      x: number,
      y: number,
      z: number,
      instance: number,
      isNote: number,
      scale: number,
      group: number,
    ) => {
      positions[cursor * 3] = x;
      positions[cursor * 3 + 1] = y;
      positions[cursor * 3 + 2] = z;
      pointData[cursor * 4] = instance;
      pointData[cursor * 4 + 1] = isNote;
      pointData[cursor * 4 + 2] = scale;
      pointData[cursor * 4 + 3] = group;
      cursor += 1;
    };

    /** y of measure ring `i`, mirrored around a gap at the equator. */
    const ringY = (i: number) => {
      const half = Math.floor(ringCount / 2);
      const step = i < half ? half - i : i - half + 1;
      return (i < half ? -1 : 1) * (GAP + step * RING_PITCH);
    };

    for (let instance = 0; instance < 2; instance += 1) {
      for (let ring = 0; ring < ringCount; ring += 1) {
        const y = ringY(ring);
        // Sorted angles, not raw ones. Points blend in buffer order, so an
        // unsorted ring interleaves near and far dots and the ring stipples
        // instead of reading as one continuous line of engraving.
        const angles = new Float32Array(ringDots);
        for (let i = 0; i < ringDots; i += 1) angles[i] = rng() * Math.PI * 2;
        angles.sort();
        for (let i = 0; i < ringDots; i += 1) {
          const a = angles[i] ?? 0;
          write(RADIUS * Math.cos(a), y, RADIUS * Math.sin(a), instance, 0, MEASURE_SCALE, 0);
        }
      }
    }

    const bandTop = GAP + Math.ceil(ringCount / 2) * RING_PITCH;
    for (let instance = 0; instance < 2; instance += 1) {
      for (let d = 0; d < dividerCount; d += 1) {
        const a = (d / dividerCount) * Math.PI * 2 + instance * 0.19;
        for (let i = 0; i < dividerDots; i += 1) {
          const t = dividerDots === 1 ? 0.5 : i / (dividerDots - 1);
          const y = -bandTop + t * bandTop * 2;
          write(RADIUS * Math.cos(a), y, RADIUS * Math.sin(a), instance, 0, MEASURE_SCALE, 0);
        }
      }
    }

    for (let instance = 0; instance < 2; instance += 1) {
      for (let g = 0; g < noteGroups; g += 1) {
        const centre = (g / noteGroups) * Math.PI * 2 + instance * 0.4;
        for (let i = 0; i < noteDots; i += 1) {
          const a = centre + (rng() - 0.5) * 0.22;
          const y = (rng() - 0.5) * 2 * bandTop;
          write(RADIUS * Math.cos(a), y, RADIUS * Math.sin(a), instance, 1, NOTE_SCALE, g);
        }
      }
    }

    const geometry = new THREE.BufferGeometry();
    geometry.setAttribute('position', new THREE.BufferAttribute(positions, 3));
    geometry.setAttribute('aPointData', new THREE.BufferAttribute(pointData, 4));

    const uniforms: Uniforms = {
      uSpin: { value: 0 },
      uElapsed: { value: 0 },
      uViewScale: { value: 1 },
      uViewportYOffset: { value: 0 },
      uPixelRatio: { value: renderer.getPixelRatio() },
      uDotScale: { value: dotScale },
      uOpacity: { value: opacity },
      uNoteInterval: { value: noteInterval },
      uGroupCount: { value: noteGroups },
      uColor: { value: new THREE.Color(color) },
      uNoteColor: { value: new THREE.Color(noteColor) },
    };

    const material = new THREE.ShaderMaterial({
      vertexShader: CYLINDER_DOT_SCORE_VERT,
      fragmentShader: CYLINDER_DOT_SCORE_FRAG,
      uniforms,
      transparent: true,
      // Both off. With depth testing on, the first dot rasterised at a given
      // pixel would win and the far wall of the cylinder would punch holes in
      // the near one, because every dot is flattened to the same z.
      depthTest: false,
      depthWrite: false,
    });

    const points = new THREE.Points(geometry, material);
    points.frustumCulled = false;
    scene.add(points);

    el.appendChild(renderer.domElement);
    renderer.domElement.style.display = 'block';
    renderer.domElement.style.width = '100%';
    renderer.domElement.style.height = '100%';

    const resize = (w: number, h: number) => {
      renderer.setSize(w, h, false);
      camera.left = -w / 2;
      camera.right = w / 2;
      camera.top = h / 2;
      camera.bottom = -h / 2;
      camera.updateProjectionMatrix();
      const scale = Math.min(w, h) * viewScale;
      uniforms.uViewScale.value = scale;
      // The stack spans 0 .. STACK_OFFSET in y; pulling the whole thing down
      // by half of that puts the pair's centre on the container's centre.
      uniforms.uViewportYOffset.value = -STACK_OFFSET * 0.5 * scale;
      uniforms.uPixelRatio.value = renderer.getPixelRatio();
    };

    const draw = (elapsed: number) => {
      uniforms.uElapsed.value = elapsed;
      uniforms.uSpin.value = elapsed * spinSpeed;
      renderer.render(scene, camera);
    };

    resize(size.current.width, size.current.height);
    stage.current = { resize, draw };
    draw(STATIC_ELAPSED);

    return () => {
      stage.current = null;
      disposeObject(scene);
      material.dispose();
      disposeRenderer(renderer);
      renderer.domElement.remove();
    };
  }, [
    ready,
    ringCount,
    ringDots,
    dividerCount,
    dividerDots,
    noteGroups,
    noteDots,
    spinSpeed,
    noteInterval,
    dotScale,
    viewScale,
    opacity,
    color,
    noteColor,
    seed,
  ]);

  useEffect(() => {
    stage.current?.resize(width, height);
    if (reduced) stage.current?.draw(STATIC_ELAPSED);
  }, [width, height, reduced]);

  useRaf((_dt, elapsed) => stage.current?.draw(elapsed), ready && !reduced && !unsupported);
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Nulls the stage ref so a queued frame cannot touch a dead renderer, disposes the geometry through `disposeObject(scene)`, disposes the material, calls `disposeRenderer` for `dispose` + `forceContextLoss` + a zeroed backing store, and removes the canvas. `useRaf` unsubscribes on unmount.

**Reduced motion.** No frame loop is opened. One frame is drawn at `uElapsed = 0.4`, which shows both cylinders at a legible yaw with the first note group lit, so the structure and the highlight convention are both visible. Neither the rotation nor the playhead advances.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Leaving `depthTest` on. Every dot is projected with z = 0, so the first fragment written at a pixel wins and the far wall of the cylinder punches holes in the near one. The whole design depends on buffer order, not on the depth buffer.
- Sorting note dots into the buffer before measure dots, or drawing them as a second object added earlier. With depth testing off, "on top" means "later in the buffer" — get it wrong and the notes are half-eaten by the rings that surround them.
- Applying the stack offset before `rotateX`. It then rotates with the model, and the two cylinders slowly drift into each other over the course of a revolution instead of staying vertically separated.
- Writing raw random angles into a ring. Blending happens in buffer order, so unsorted angles interleave near and far dots and the ring visibly stipples rather than reading as a continuous engraved line.
- Driving the playhead from React state and an interval. It re-renders the tree once per beat, and the highlight lands one frame after the beat because the uniform write happens in a commit rather than in the frame loop — deriving it from `uElapsed` in the shader avoids both.
- Rebuilding the buffer when the container resizes. Model space is size-independent; only `uViewScale` and `uViewportYOffset` change, so a reflow costs two uniform writes rather than a dropped GL context.
- Setting `frustumCulled` at its default. Positions are unit-scale around the origin and the real placement happens in the shader, so three's bounding sphere does not describe what is on screen.

## Notes

- The two cylinders are "instances" only in the conceptual sense — this is one non-instanced `Points` with an index in an attribute, which is cheaper than instancing for a case where every vertex differs anyway.
- Total dot count is `2 * (ringCount * ringDots + dividerCount * dividerDots + noteGroups * noteDots)`, about 6100 at the defaults, in one draw call.

## Definition of done

Two stacked cylinders of dots turn at a constant rate, showing different faces to the viewer. Dots on the far side are visibly smaller and dimmer than those on the near side, and no dot ever pops in front of one it should be behind. A cluster of larger note dots lights every 1.2 seconds and cycles around the cylinder. Resize the container and the piece rescales without a flicker. With reduced motion it holds a single legible frame.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Cylinder Gallery Drum

A flat PlaneGeometry per item, all sharing one compiled program, each bent around a common cylinder by its own uniform. The camera never moves and the CPU never touches a vertex: scrolling changes one float, `position`, and every plane recomputes its angle, its height and its focus weight from that single scalar. Because the ring offset is the shortest signed distance on a circular index, the list is genuinely endless in both directions with no clones and no rebuilding.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Nineteen planes wrapped around a drum in the vertex shader, spun by wheel or scroll, focus falling off from centre.

- Category: webgl
- Runtime cost: webgl
- Dependencies: three@^0.185.1, gsap@^3.15.0, lenis@^1.3.11

## How it works

1. The vertex shader treats a vertex's own x as an arc offset: `angle = uSpiralAngle + position.x`, then `pos.x = uRadius * sin(angle)` and `pos.z = uRadius * cos(angle)`, so one world unit of plane width wraps exactly one radian of drum. `pos.y = sin(position.y)` pulls the top and bottom edges in, which turns a rolled sheet into a barrel.
2. Per frame and per plane, `wrappedOffset(i, position, count)` returns the shortest signed distance from that plane to the focused index — the value that makes index 0 sit one step before index 18 rather than eighteen steps after it. That offset drives `uSpiralAngle = (offset / count) * 2π * turns`, the vertical stack `y = -offset * spacing`, and the focus term.
3. Focus is `gaussian(offset)` = `exp(-offset²)`: 1.0 at the centre, 0.368 one step out, 0.018 two, 0.0001 three. The fragment shader mixes toward luminance and dims by that weight, so attention falls off continuously instead of one plane being flagged "selected".
4. A single `uIntro` scalar lerps between two complete layouts inside the shader — `mix(rowPos, ringPos, uIntro)` — where `rowPos` is a flat facing row and `ringPos` is the drum. Every intermediate value is a valid frame, and the CPU lerps the mesh x/y positions with the same scalar so the two layouts stay consistent.
5. Signed scroll velocity feeds `uDeform`, which adds `sin(position.y * 3.0 + 100.0) * uDeform * 0.07` to z and `sin(position.x * 3.0) * uDeform * 0.04` to y. It samples `position` — the original flat coordinates — not the already-bent `pos`, so the ripple is locked to the picture and reads as the image flexing rather than the drum wobbling.
6. Pointer proximity is measured inside the vertex shader by projecting each vertex once as a probe (`ndc = probe.xy / probe.w`), taking `exp(-mouseDist² * 5.0)`, lifting z by half of it and passing it to the fragment shader, which pushes the centred UV outward by the same weight so the bump also magnifies — a lens, not a bump.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `PLANE_WIDTH / PLANE_HEIGHT = 1 / 1.95`
  Width 1 because the bend uses the vertex's raw x as radians — at width 1 each plane spans exactly 1 rad of the drum, which is the whole reason no trigonometry is needed on the CPU. Height must stay under 2π/3 or `sin(position.y)` leaves its monotonic range and the barrel folds its own edges back through the surface.
- `CAMERA_FOV / CAMERA_Z = 45 / 5`
  The camera never animates, so these only set how much drum is in shot. Below ~35° the ring flattens into a row and the depth cue vanishes; above ~60° the near plane balloons and the barrel curve reads as a keystone error.
- `OVERSCAN = 1.12`
  The cover-fit UV is divided by this, zooming the crop in 12%. At exactly 1.0 the wave and the bulge push vertices past the sampled region and the texture's own clamped border smears along the edge. Beyond ~1.25 the crop eats the subject.
- `segments = 64`
  The bend is evaluated per vertex, so subdivision *is* the curve. Below ~24 the drum visibly becomes a folded card and the mouse bulge turns into a triangular tent; past ~128 you are paying vertex cost for a curve the pixel grid cannot resolve.
- `POSITION_SMOOTHING = 0.0006`
  Fraction of remaining distance left after one second. Larger (slower) and the drum lags visibly behind the wheel; much smaller and the velocity spike that drives `uDeform` never has time to build, so the wave disappears.
- `SNAP_DELAY_MS = 170`
  Idle time before the drum eases to a whole index. Under ~120 ms it fires between the discrete events of a single trackpad flick and fights the gesture; over ~250 ms the gallery feels like it forgot to settle.
- `MAX_DEFORM / DEFORM_PER_INDEX = 1.5 / 0.42`
  Deform is clamped to ±1.5 because the shader multiplies it by 0.07 world units — past that the planes intersect each other and the far side of the drum pokes through the near side. 0.42 sets how many index-steps per second count as full deflection.
- `RADIUS_VELOCITY_GAIN = 0.5`
  The drum widens up to 50% at full speed, which is what sells inertia. Above ~0.8 the nearest plane crosses the camera's near plane during a fast flick and clips away.
- `gaussian falloff = 1 (exp(-offset²))`
  A falloff of 1 keeps the immediate neighbours legible at 0.37 while the third plane out is effectively gone. Raising it dims the neighbours to black and the ring loses its context; lowering it flattens every plane to the same weight.
- `renderOrder scale = -worldZ * 1000`
  Reconstructed drum depth, scaled up so it survives rounding to an integer sort key. At a smaller scale adjacent planes collapse into the same bucket and flicker between frames.

## API

```ts
function CylinderGallery(props: { items: CylinderGalleryItem[]; drive?: "pointer" | "page"; radius?: number; turns?: number; spacing?: number; segments?: number; pixelsPerIndex?: number; opacity?: number; paint?: (ctx: CanvasRenderingContext2D, item: CylinderGalleryItem, index: number, size: { width: number; height: number }) => void; onSelect?: (item: CylinderGalleryItem, index: number) => void; onFocusChange?: (item: CylinderGalleryItem, index: number) => void; className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `items: CylinderGalleryItem[]`
  `{ id, title, meta?, hue? }` per plane. One mesh and one generated texture each.
- `drive: "pointer" | "page"` — default `"pointer"`
  Wheel and drag inside the component, or document scroll via a shared infinite Lenis.
- `radius: number` — default `2`
  Drum radius in world units, before the velocity widening.
- `turns: number` — default `3`
  Full revolutions the ring spans across the whole list.
- `spacing: number` — default `0.8`
  World units of vertical travel per index step.
- `segments: number` — default `64`
  Plane subdivisions per axis. This is the resolution of the bend.
- `pixelsPerIndex: number` — default `240`
  Document scroll pixels per index step, in `page` mode only.
- `opacity: number` — default `1`
  Global alpha multiplier applied before the focus falloff.
- `paint: (ctx, item, index, size) => void`
  Override the generated plate. Receives a 2D context for a 512x1024 canvas.
- `onSelect: (item, index) => void`
  Tap on the drum. A drag never counts as a tap.
- `onFocusChange: (item, index) => void`
  Fires when a different index takes the centre.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the wrapper via `cn`.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
export function CylinderGallery({
  items,
  drive = 'pointer',
  radius = 2,
  turns = 3,
  spacing = 0.8,
  segments = 64,
  pixelsPerIndex = 240,
  opacity = 1,
  paint,
  onSelect,
  onFocusChange,
  className,
}: CylinderGalleryProps) {
  const host = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const stage = useRef<Stage | null>(null);

  const { width, height } = useResizeObserver(host);
  const { inView } = useInView(host, { threshold: 0 });
  const visible = useVisibility();
  const reduced = useReducedMotion();
  const pointer = useSmoothPointer({ target: host, smoothing: 0.0015 });

  // `hasWebGL` touches `document`, so it cannot run during render without
  // disagreeing with the server. Start optimistic and correct after mount:
  // both renders then agree and nothing hydrates twice.
  const [supported, setSupported] = useState(true);
  useEffect(() => setSupported(hasWebGL()), []);

  const [focused, setFocused] = useState(0);

  const position = useRef(0);
  const target = useRef(0);
  const velocity = useRef(0);
  const intro = useRef(0);
  const strength = useRef(0);
  const hovered = useRef(false);
  const focusedRef = useRef(0);
  const snapTimer = useRef<ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null>(null);
  const snapTween = useRef<Tween | null>(null);

  // Everything the frame loop reads but must not resubscribe on. Written on
  // every render, read once per frame; the loop itself never re-creates.
  const live = useRef({ radius, turns, spacing, opacity, drive, pixelsPerIndex, items, onSelect, onFocusChange });
  live.current = { radius, turns, spacing, opacity, drive, pixelsPerIndex, items, onSelect, onFocusChange };

  // Rebuilding the scene is expensive, so it is keyed on what actually changes
  // the meshes — identity, label and hue — not on the array's reference, which
  // is new on every render for any caller who writes the list inline.
  const itemsKey = items.map((item) => `${item.id}:${item.title}:${item.hue ?? ''}`).join('|');

  const lenis = useLenis({ infinite: true, enabled: drive === 'page' });

  const killSnap = useCallback(() => {
    if (snapTimer.current !== null) {
      clearTimeout(snapTimer.current);
      snapTimer.current = null;
    }
    snapTween.current?.kill();
    snapTween.current = null;
  }, []);

  const scheduleSnap = useCallback(() => {
    if (snapTimer.current !== null) clearTimeout(snapTimer.current);
    snapTimer.current = setTimeout(() => {
      snapTimer.current = null;
      // Snap the TARGET, not the position: the frame loop keeps damping
      // toward it, so the settle stays one continuous motion instead of a
      // second animation fighting the first.
      snapTween.current = gsap.to(target, {
        current: Math.round(target.current),
        duration: SNAP_DURATION,
        ease: 'power3.out',
      });
    }, SNAP_DELAY_MS);
  }, []);

  /* ---- scene construction ------------------------------------------------ */

  const ready = width > 1 && height > 1 && supported;

  useEffect(() => {
    const el = host.current;
    if (!el || !ready || items.length === 0) return;

    const renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer({ antialias: true, alpha: true });
    // Capped, not raw. A 3x phone with an uncapped ratio pays 9x the fill rate
    // for a difference nobody can see.
    renderer.setPixelRatio(pixelRatio());
    renderer.setSize(el.clientWidth, el.clientHeight, false);
    renderer.setClearColor(0x000000, 0);
    renderer.domElement.style.display = 'block';
    renderer.domElement.style.width = '100%';
    renderer.domElement.style.height = '100%';
    el.appendChild(renderer.domElement);

    const scene = new THREE.Scene();
    const camera = new THREE.PerspectiveCamera(
      CAMERA_FOV,
      el.clientWidth / Math.max(el.clientHeight, 1),
      0.1,
      100,
    );
    camera.position.z = CAMERA_Z;

    // One geometry for every plane. The bend is per-vertex, so the mesh has to
    // be dense enough that the curve reads as a curve: below ~24 segments the
    // drum visibly becomes a folded card.
    const geometry = new THREE.PlaneGeometry(PLANE_WIDTH, PLANE_HEIGHT, segments, segments);
    const planeAspect = PLANE_WIDTH / PLANE_HEIGHT;
    const paintItem = paint ?? paintPlate;
    const maxAnisotropy = Math.min(4, renderer.capabilities.getMaxAnisotropy());

    const planes: Plane[] = items.map((item, index) => {
      const canvas = document.createElement('canvas');
      canvas.width = TEXTURE_WIDTH;
      canvas.height = TEXTURE_HEIGHT;
      const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d');
      if (ctx) paintItem(ctx, item, index, { width: TEXTURE_WIDTH, height: TEXTURE_HEIGHT });

      const texture = new THREE.CanvasTexture(canvas);
      // sRGB in, sRGB out. Skip this and the plates render noticeably darker
      // than the CSS colours sitting next to them.
      texture.colorSpace = THREE.SRGBColorSpace;
      texture.anisotropy = maxAnisotropy;
      texture.needsUpdate = true;

      const uniforms: PlaneUniforms = {
        uTexture: { value: texture },
        uTextureAspect: { value: TEXTURE_WIDTH / TEXTURE_HEIGHT },
        uPlaneAspect: { value: planeAspect },
        uOverscan: { value: OVERSCAN },
        uSpiralAngle: { value: 0 },
        uRadius: { value: radius },
        uIntro: { value: 0 },
        uFocus: { value: 1 },
        uOpacity: { value: opacity },
        uDeform: { value: 0 },
        uMouseNdc: { value: new THREE.Vector2(0, 0) },
        uMouseStrength: { value: 0 },
      };

      // A material per mesh, because every plane needs its own spiralAngle,
      // radius and focus. three keys its program cache on the shader source,
      // so all of these share one compiled program regardless.
      const material = new THREE.ShaderMaterial({
        vertexShader: cylinderGalleryVertexShader,
        fragmentShader: cylinderGalleryFragmentShader,
        uniforms,
        transparent: true,
        side: THREE.DoubleSide,
        // Painted strictly back to front via renderOrder below, so neither
        // depth write nor depth test has anything to contribute — and both
        // would be wrong anyway, since the depth they compare is the depth of
        // a mesh the CPU thinks is still flat at the origin.
        depthWrite: false,
        depthTest: false,
      });

      const mesh = new THREE.Mesh(geometry, material);
      // The CPU-side geometry is a flat plane at mesh.position; the shape you
      // can actually see is somewhere else entirely. Frustum culling compares
      // against that stale bounding sphere and blanks planes that are plainly
      // on screen.
      mesh.frustumCulled = false;
      scene.add(mesh);
      return { mesh, uniforms, texture };
    });

    stage.current = { renderer, scene, camera, geometry, planes };
    renderer.render(scene, camera);

    return () => {
      stage.current = null;
      for (const plane of planes) {
        scene.remove(plane.mesh);
        // disposeObject walks a material's own properties looking for
        // textures. These live inside `uniforms`, two levels down, so it will
        // never find them — they have to be released by hand.
        plane.texture.dispose();
      }
      disposeObject(scene);
      geometry.dispose();
      // dispose() frees GPU objects and leaves the context alive. Only
      // forceContextLoss, which disposeRenderer calls, hands it back.
      disposeRenderer(renderer);
      renderer.domElement.remove();
    };
    // `items` is read through the key; `radius`/`opacity` only seed uniforms
    // the frame loop overwrites immediately.
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, [ready, itemsKey, segments, paint]);

  /* ---- size ------------------------------------------------------------- */

  useEffect(() => {
    const current = stage.current;
    if (!current || width < 1 || height < 1) return;
    current.renderer.setPixelRatio(pixelRatio());
    // `false` — the canvas is sized by CSS at 100%/100%; letting three write
    // inline pixel dimensions makes it fight the flex parent on every resize.
    current.renderer.setSize(width, height, false);
    current.camera.aspect = width / height;
    current.camera.updateProjectionMatrix();
  }, [width, height]);

  /* ---- intro morph ------------------------------------------------------- */

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!ready) return;
    if (reduced) {
      intro.current = 1;
      return;
    }
    intro.current = 0;
    const tween = gsap.to(intro, {
      current: 1,
      duration: INTRO_DURATION,
      delay: INTRO_DELAY,
      ease: 'power3.inOut',
    });
    return () => {
      tween.kill();
    };
  }, [ready, reduced]);

  /* ---- input ------------------------------------------------------------- */

  useEffect(() => {
    const el = host.current;
    if (!el || drive !== 'pointer') return;

    const onWheel = (event: WheelEvent) => {
      // Non-passive on purpose: without preventDefault the drum spins AND the
      // page scrolls under it, which reads as two competing gestures.
      event.preventDefault();
      killSnap();
      target.current += event.deltaY * WHEEL_INDEX_PER_PIXEL;
      scheduleSnap();
    };

    el.addEventListener('wheel', onWheel, { passive: false });
    return () => el.removeEventListener('wheel', onWheel);
  }, [drive, killSnap, scheduleSnap]);

  useEffect(() => {
    const el = host.current;
    if (!el) return;
    const enter = () => {
      hovered.current = true;
    };
    const leave = () => {
      hovered.current = false;
    };
    el.addEventListener('pointerenter', enter);
    el.addEventListener('pointerleave', leave);
    return () => {
      el.removeEventListener('pointerenter', enter);
      el.removeEventListener('pointerleave', leave);
    };
  }, []);

  useDrag(host, {
    enabled: drive === 'pointer',
    onDragStart: killSnap,
    onDrag: (state) => {
      target.current -= state.deltaY * DRAG_INDEX_PER_PIXEL;
    },
    onDragEnd: (_state, moved) => {
      if (!moved) {
        const { items: list, onSelect: select } = live.current;
        const index = wrapIndex(Math.round(position.current), list.length);
        const item = list[index];
        if (item) select?.(item, index);
      }
      scheduleSnap();
    },
  });

  useEffect(() => killSnap, [killSnap]);

  /* ---- the frame --------------------------------------------------------- */

  useRaf(
    (dt) => {
      const current = stage.current;
      if (!current) return;
      const {
        radius: baseRadius,
        turns: baseTurns,
        spacing: baseSpacing,
        opacity: alpha,
        drive: mode,
        pixelsPerIndex: perIndex,
        items: list,
        onFocusChange: notify,
      } = live.current;

      const count = current.planes.length;
      if (count === 0) return;

      if (mode === 'page') {
        const instance = lenis.current;
        if (instance) target.current = instance.scroll / Math.max(perIndex, 1);
      }

      const previous = position.current;
      position.current = damp(position.current, target.current, POSITION_SMOOTHING, dt);

      // Index steps per second, smoothed by the same damp that produced the
      // position, so the wave can never lead the geometry it is bending.
      const instant = dt > 0 ? (position.current - previous) / dt : 0;
      velocity.current = damp(velocity.current, instant, 0.002, dt);
      const normalized = clamp(velocity.current / VELOCITY_REFERENCE, -1, 1);

      strength.current = damp(
        strength.current,
        hovered.current && !reduced ? 1 : 0,
        STRENGTH_SMOOTHING,
        dt,
      );

      const s = intro.current;
      const speed = Math.abs(normalized);
      const liveRadius = baseRadius * (1 + RADIUS_VELOCITY_GAIN * speed);
      const liveSpacing = baseSpacing * (1 + SPACING_VELOCITY_GAIN * speed);
      const angularScale = 1 + ANGULAR_VELOCITY_GAIN * speed;
      const deform = reduced
        ? 0
        : clamp(velocity.current * DEFORM_PER_INDEX, -MAX_DEFORM, MAX_DEFORM);

      // The flat-row layout spans the frustum's visible WIDTH at z = 0. Sizing
      // it from window.innerWidth, or from the visible height, leaves the row
      // short on wide viewports and clipped on narrow ones.
      const visibleWidth =
        2 * Math.tan((CAMERA_FOV * Math.PI) / 360) * CAMERA_Z * current.camera.aspect * 0.86;
      const step = visibleWidth / Math.max(count - 1, 1);
      const rowWidth = (count - 1) * step;

      const mx = pointer.current.active ? pointer.current.ndcX : 0;
      const my = pointer.current.active ? pointer.current.ndcY : 0;

      for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        const plane = current.planes[i];
        if (!plane) continue;

        // The one call that makes a finite array behave like an infinite ring:
        // item 0 is one step BEFORE item 18, not eighteen steps after it.
        const offset = wrappedOffset(i, position.current, count);
        const angle = (offset / count) * Math.PI * 2 * baseTurns * angularScale;
        const y = -offset * liveSpacing;

        plane.mesh.position.x = (i * step - rowWidth / 2) * (1 - s);
        plane.mesh.position.y = y * s;
        plane.mesh.scale.setScalar(lerp(0.62, 1, s));

        const u = plane.uniforms;
        u.uSpiralAngle.value = angle;
        u.uRadius.value = liveRadius;
        u.uIntro.value = s;
        u.uDeform.value = deform;
        u.uOpacity.value = alpha;
        u.uMouseStrength.value = strength.current;
        u.uMouseNdc.value.set(mx, my);
        // exp(-d²): 1.000 at the centre, 0.368 one step out, 0.018 two, 0.0001
        // three. Continuous, branchless, and the reason the drum reads as
        // analogue rather than as a list with a selected row.
        u.uFocus.value = lerp(1, gaussian(offset), s);

        // Transparent meshes are sorted by three using the CPU position, which
        // for this drum is (0, y, 0) for every plane. Reconstructing the depth
        // the shader will actually produce and painting back to front is the
        // only way the far side of the ring stays behind the near side.
        const worldZ = liveRadius * Math.cos(angle) * s;
        plane.mesh.renderOrder = Math.round(-worldZ * 1000);
      }

      const nextFocus = wrapIndex(Math.round(position.current), count);
      if (nextFocus !== focusedRef.current) {
        focusedRef.current = nextFocus;
        setFocused(nextFocus);
        const item = list[nextFocus];
        if (item) notify?.(item, nextFocus);
      }

      current.renderer.render(current.scene, current.camera);
    },
    ready && inView && visible,
  );
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Removes the wheel and pointerenter/pointerleave listeners, kills the intro tween and any pending snap timeout plus its tween, removes every mesh from the scene, disposes each `CanvasTexture` by hand (they sit inside `material.uniforms`, where `disposeObject` cannot reach), runs `disposeObject` for the geometries and materials, disposes the shared geometry, then `disposeRenderer` — `setAnimationLoop(null)`, `dispose()`, `forceContextLoss()` — and removes the canvas from the DOM. The frame loop reads a stage ref that is nulled first, so a queued frame after teardown is a no-op rather than a null context throw.

**Reduced motion.** The intro morph is skipped — `uIntro` is set to 1 on mount, so the drum is simply already assembled. The velocity wave is pinned to 0 and the pointer bulge never engages, so the surface stays flat. Navigation still works and still eases: wheel, drag and the snap-to-index tween are unchanged, because the user asked for less motion, not for a gallery that cannot move.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Scaling `uRadius` from 0 to animate the intro. At radius 0 every vertex of every plane lands on the origin, so the "flat" state is nineteen invisible slivers stacked in one spot. Lerp between two position vectors — `mix(rowPos, ringPos, uIntro)` — and the flat state is a real layout you can hold.
- Leaving `frustumCulled` at its default. The CPU-side geometry is still a flat plane sitting at `mesh.position`; the visible shape is somewhere else entirely. three culls against that stale bounding sphere and planes that are plainly on screen blink out at the edges.
- Trusting three's transparency sort. It orders transparent meshes by their object position, which for this drum is `(0, y, 0)` for every single plane, so the far side of the ring paints over the near side at random. Reconstruct the depth the shader will produce (`radius * cos(angle) * intro`) and set `renderOrder` from it each frame.
- Expecting `disposeObject` to free the plate textures. It scans a material's own properties for anything with `isTexture`; these textures live two levels down inside `material.uniforms`, so it never sees them and nineteen 512x1024 canvases stay resident on the GPU after unmount. They are disposed explicitly from a tracked list.
- Calling `renderer.dispose()` and stopping there. That releases GPU objects but keeps the WebGL context alive; Chromium caps a renderer process at roughly 16 and silently kills the oldest, so a docs page that mounts several of these blanks the ones above it. `disposeRenderer` calls `forceContextLoss`.
- Attaching the wheel listener passively. Without `preventDefault` the drum spins and the host page scrolls at the same time, which reads as two gestures fighting; the listener is registered with `{ passive: false }`.
- Sampling the deformation wave from the already-bent `pos` instead of the original `position`. The ripple then travels with the drum rotation rather than staying pinned to the image, and the effect looks like a rendering fault instead of the picture flexing.
- Sizing the flat-row layout from `window.innerWidth`. The row has to span the frustum's visible width at z = 0, which is `2 * tan(fov/2) * cameraZ * aspect` — the container width in pixels has no fixed relationship to that, so the row overshoots on wide viewports and clips on narrow ones.
- Omitting `#include <colorspace_fragment>` from a `ShaderMaterial`. three only injects output conversion into its own materials, so raw linear values ship into an sRGB framebuffer and the plates render visibly washed out next to the CSS around them.
- Rebuilding the scene when the `items` array identity changes. Any caller who writes the list inline hands over a new array every render, which would tear down nineteen textures and a GL context on every keystroke. The setup effect keys on a string built from id, title and hue.

## Notes

- Textures are drawn at mount to a 512x1024 canvas per item — a hue ramp, hairline bands and a numeral. The bands are not decoration: a smooth gradient hides every deformation the shader applies, so the plate needs structure for the wave and the bulge to bend.
- All nineteen materials are separate `ShaderMaterial` instances because each needs its own uniforms, but three keys its program cache on the shader source, so they share a single compiled program.
- `drive: "page"` opts into a shared refcounted Lenis with `infinite: true`, which is the technique in its original form — the gallery *is* the page. The default `drive: "pointer"` keeps every gesture inside the component's own box.

## Definition of done

On mount the planes start as a flat row facing you and curl into a drum over about 1.6 s. Wheel or drag spins it endlessly in both directions with no seam and no jump at the ends; stop moving and it eases to centre one plane. The centred plane is full colour and the neighbours fade toward grey within two steps. Flick hard and the images ripple, the drum widens, and the ripple runs opposite ways depending on direction. Move the pointer over a plane and a soft lens follows it, magnifying rather than just denting. Unmount from React DevTools and the canvas leaves the DOM with no context-lost warning; mount and unmount twenty times and no context is dropped. With `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the drum is already assembled on the first frame and neither the ripple nor the lens ever appears.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.
