# Build: Stroke-To-Fill Hover Rows

A list of large type where every row is an outline with a ghost of fill, and the hovered row materialises: the stroke drops to zero width, the fill goes to full `currentColor`, and the row steps 12px to the right while its siblings recede. The row does not light up, it becomes solid. Everything is CSS, so nothing but the compositor runs on hover.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

An index of outlined type where the hovered row fills in solid, drops its stroke, and steps sideways.

- Category: text
- Runtime cost: css
- Dependencies: none beyond React

## How it works

1. Two properties carry the effect, and they are separate on purpose: `-webkit-text-stroke-width` goes 1px to 0, and `-webkit-text-fill-color` goes from a ghost of `currentColor` to `currentColor` itself.
2. `-webkit-text-fill-color` overrides `color` for the glyph interior only, which is what lets the outline stay at `currentColor` while the inside is nearly transparent. Doing this with `color` alone is impossible — `color` is also what `currentColor` resolves to, so fading the fill fades the stroke with it and the row just dims.
3. The ghost is `color-mix(in oklch, currentColor var(--kx-sf-ghost, 16%), transparent)` rather than a literal `rgba`. It inherits the surrounding text colour, so one component is correct on a dark page and a light one, and mixing in oklch keeps the 16% step perceptually even instead of clumping toward black the way sRGB alpha does.
4. The three tunables are custom properties set on the `<ul>` from props (`--kx-sf-stroke`, `--kx-sf-ghost`, `--kx-sf-nudge`), so per-instance configuration needs no extra class and no extra rule.
5. Sibling dimming is scoped to the list's own hover: `.kinetic-sf-list:hover .kinetic-sf-row:not(:hover) { opacity: 0.45 }`. Scoping to the list is what makes the resting state "all rows equal" rather than "all rows dimmed".
6. Every hover rule is duplicated for `:focus-visible`. Each row is a real `<a>` or `<button>` inside an `<li>`, so keyboard traversal produces the same state change — without it a keyboard user tabbing ten identical outlines has no idea where they are.
7. The stylesheet is emitted once through React 19's `<style href precedence>` hoisting, so any number of lists on a page share one rule set.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `STROKE_WIDTH = 1`
  Pixels of outline at rest. At the 28-72px type this component targets, 1px is a hairline that still reads as a complete letterform; 2px starts to close up counters in tighter faces and the row looks bold rather than outlined.
- `GHOST = 16`
  Percent of `currentColor` mixed into the resting fill. At 0 the glyph interiors are fully transparent and the type dissolves into whatever is behind it; past ~30% the resting and hovered states are too close for the transition to register.
- `NUDGE = 12`
  Pixels the hovered row steps right. Enough to be unmistakable next to a static neighbour; past ~24px the row visibly leaves the left margin of the list and the alignment looks broken.
- `transition duration / curve = 380ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`
  A strong ease-out. The row arrives quickly and settles, which matches the pointer having already stopped. A symmetric ease at this duration lags the cursor noticeably on a fast pass down a ten-row list.
- `sibling opacity = 0.45`
  Enough separation that the hovered row is unambiguous, while the others stay legible — dimming to 0.2 turns a browsable index into a spotlight and hides the thing the user is scanning for.

## API

```ts
function StrokeToFillRows(props: { items: StrokeToFillItem[]; strokeWidth?: number; ghost?: number; nudge?: number; className?: string; onSelect?: (item: StrokeToFillItem, index: number) => void }): JSX.Element
```

- `items: StrokeToFillItem[]`
  Rows. Each has a `label`, an optional `meta` node for right-hand metadata, and an optional `href`.
- `strokeWidth: number` — default `1`
  Outline thickness in px at rest.
- `ghost: number` — default `16`
  Resting fill as a percentage of `currentColor`.
- `nudge: number` — default `12`
  Pixels the hovered row steps right.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the `<ul>` via `cn`.
- `onSelect: (item: StrokeToFillItem, index: number) => void`
  Called when a row without an `href` is activated.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
const ROWS_CSS = `
.kinetic-sf-title {
  -webkit-text-stroke: var(--kx-sf-stroke, 1px) currentColor;
  -webkit-text-fill-color: color-mix(in oklch, currentColor var(--kx-sf-ghost, 16%), transparent);
  transition:
    -webkit-text-fill-color 380ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1),
    -webkit-text-stroke-width 380ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1),
    transform 380ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1);
  transform: translate3d(0, 0, 0);
}
/* :focus-visible alongside :hover, always. A keyboard user tabbing an index
   of ten rows otherwise sees ten identical outlines and no current position. */
.kinetic-sf-row:hover .kinetic-sf-title,
.kinetic-sf-row:focus-visible .kinetic-sf-title {
  -webkit-text-fill-color: currentColor;
  -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px;
  transform: translate3d(var(--kx-sf-nudge, 12px), 0, 0);
}
/* Everything that is not the hovered row recedes. Scoped to the list's own
   hover so the resting state is all rows equal, not all rows dimmed. */
.kinetic-sf-list:hover .kinetic-sf-row:not(:hover) {
  opacity: 0.45;
}
.kinetic-sf-row {
  transition: opacity 380ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1);
}
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  /* The stroke-to-fill swap is a state change, not motion, and it stays. The
     12 px lateral travel is motion, and it goes. */
  .kinetic-sf-row:hover .kinetic-sf-title,
  .kinetic-sf-row:focus-visible .kinetic-sf-title {
    transform: none;
  }
}
`;

export interface StrokeToFillItem {
  label: string;
  /** Right-hand metadata: a year, a category, a count. */
  meta?: ReactNode;
  href?: string;
}

export interface StrokeToFillRowsProps {
  items: StrokeToFillItem[];
  /** Outline thickness in px at rest. */
  strokeWidth?: number;
  /** Resting fill, as a percentage of `currentColor`. */
  ghost?: number;
  /** Pixels the hovered row steps right. */
  nudge?: number;
  className?: string;
  onSelect?: (item: StrokeToFillItem, index: number) => void;
}

const STROKE_WIDTH = 1;
const GHOST = 16;
const NUDGE = 12;

export function StrokeToFillRows({
  items,
  strokeWidth = STROKE_WIDTH,
  ghost = GHOST,
  nudge = NUDGE,
  className,
  onSelect,
}: StrokeToFillRowsProps) {
  return (
    <>
      <style href="kinetic-stroke-to-fill" precedence="medium">
        {ROWS_CSS}
      </style>
      <ul
        className={cn('kinetic-sf-list w-full', className)}
        style={
          {
            '--kx-sf-stroke': `${strokeWidth}px`,
            '--kx-sf-ghost': `${ghost}%`,
            '--kx-sf-nudge': `${nudge}px`,
          } as CSSProperties
        }
      >
        {items.map((item, i) => {
          const inner = (
            <>
              <span className="kinetic-sf-title block text-[clamp(28px,5.5vw,72px)] leading-[1.06] tracking-[-0.03em]">
                {item.label}
              </span>
              {item.meta ? (
                <span className="meta shrink-0 pt-[0.35em]">{item.meta}</span>
              ) : null}
            </>
          );

          return (
            <li key={`${item.label}-${i}`} className="border-b border-line">
              {item.href ? (
                <a
                  href={item.href}
                  className="kinetic-sf-row flex w-full items-start justify-between gap-6 py-[0.35em] text-left outline-none"
                >
                  {inner}
                </a>
              ) : (
                <button
                  type="button"
                  onClick={() => onSelect?.(item, i)}
                  className="kinetic-sf-row flex w-full items-start justify-between gap-6 py-[0.35em] text-left outline-none"
                >
                  {inner}
                </button>
              )}
            </li>
          );
        })}
      </ul>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Nothing to clean up: no effect, no listener, no timer. Unmounting removes the list; React's `<style precedence>` hoisting owns the shared rule set.

**Reduced motion.** The stroke-to-fill swap is a state change, not motion, so it is kept in full — the hovered row still fills solid and its siblings still recede. Only the 12px lateral travel is removed, via `transform: none` in a `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` block. The rows are never left unreadable.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Trying to build this with `color` alone. Fading the fill fades the stroke with it because `currentColor` resolves to the same value, so the row dims instead of filling.
- Transitioning the `-webkit-text-stroke` shorthand. Shorthands are not independently interpolable here; transition `-webkit-text-stroke-width` explicitly or the stroke snaps off in one frame while the fill glides.
- Hardcoding the resting fill as `rgba(255,255,255,0.16)`. The component is then wrong the moment it lands on a light background, and wrong again in an inverted section of the same page.
- Mixing the ghost in sRGB. The intermediate steps clump toward black, so the resting fill on a mid-tone accent looks muddy rather than faint.
- Dimming siblings without scoping to `.kinetic-sf-list:hover`. Every row is then permanently at 0.45 and the "recede" has nothing to recede from.
- Styling `:hover` and forgetting `:focus-visible`. Keyboard users get ten identical outlines and no indication of the current row, which is a genuine accessibility failure and not just a polish gap.
- Animating `left` or `margin-left` for the nudge. Both trigger layout on every row of a large-type index; `translate3d` stays on the compositor.

## Notes

- No text splitting and no motion library: this is a state change on a whole row, so imposing a splitter or GSAP on the consumer for a CSS-cost effect would be pure overhead.
- `-webkit-text-stroke` is unprefixed-less by history but supported in every current engine including Firefox and Safari. There is no standards-track alternative that composites the same way.
- Rows render as `<a>` when `href` is given and as `<button>` otherwise, so the list is keyboard-traversable either way without a `tabIndex` hack.

## Definition of done

Hover a row: the outline thins to nothing as the glyph interiors fill to full colour, and the row slides 12px right while the others fade back. Tab through with a keyboard and the same state appears on the focused row. Flip the page between light and dark themes and the resting ghost fill is still faintly visible in both, without editing the component. With reduced motion enabled the fill still happens and the row does not move.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.


---

# Build: Superellipse Text Avoidance

The headline is real DOM on top of an instanced particle field, and the field is pushed out of a 6-norm superellipse fitted to the headline's measured rect. Interior particles are remapped into a band hugging the shape rather than clamped onto it, so the hole has a bright rim instead of a pile-up. The same avoidance function runs a second time at exponent 2 for the damped pointer, because a disc is a superellipse with a lower exponent.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

A particle field that flows around the headline, held off by a 6-norm superellipse fitted to the measured text box.

- Category: webgl
- Runtime cost: webgl
- Dependencies: ogl@^1.0.11

## How it works

1. The avoidance region is `pow(pow(|nx|, e) + pow(|ny|, e), 1/e) < 1` in the rect's own normalised space. At e = 2 that is an ellipse, at e = 6 a squircle, at e = 20 effectively a box. Six is the useful one: a circle around a wide headline clears a large empty halo past the ends of the line, and a box has four corner discontinuities that crease the field along straight lines.
2. Interior radii are REMAPPED, not clamped. `mapped = 1 + whip * min(r, 1 + whip) / (1 + whip) + max(r - (1 + whip), 0)` compresses [0, 1 + whip] into [1, 1 + whip] and is the identity beyond it. Clamping instead maps a whole area onto a curve, so every interior particle lands on the outline and the shape is drawn as one infinitely dense line with an empty interior behind it.
3. The displacement is `half * (n / max(r, 1e-3)) * (mapped - r)` — divided by a floor rather than normalized. A particle at the exact centre has no direction and `normalize()` returns NaN there, which propagates into `gl_Position` and drops the whole instance rather than one component. A lattice puts particles exactly on both axes on the first frame, so this case is reached immediately, not never.
4. `pow()` is undefined for a negative base and for zero raised to a non-positive power, and a symmetric field hits both. The norm takes `abs()` first and adds 1e-5, which costs nothing and removes an entire class of driver-dependent black frames.
5. The rect is measured, never passed in. `getBoundingClientRect()` on the text node and on the host produce four uv numbers; a ResizeObserver on the text node plus `document.fonts.ready` keeps them in step through a rewrap, a font swap and a container resize. A hand-tuned rect is wrong on the first webfont load and wrong again on the first narrow viewport.
6. The text rect is deliberately NOT aspect-corrected, because it was measured in element space and has to stay there or it stops agreeing with the letters. The pointer disc IS aspect-corrected, because it is a shape in screen space and an uncorrected one is a visible ellipse on any non-square container. The two live in the same shader and want opposite treatment.
7. Displaced particles brighten and grow slightly, tinted toward a third colour. Without it the field is just a hole and the exponent is invisible; with it the squircle is legible as a rim, which is the only on-screen evidence that the shape is not a box.
8. The scatter is a jittered lattice, then shuffled. Uniform random has clumps and voids at this population, and once the avoidance opens a real hole the accidental voids read as more holes. The shuffle matters because the instanced count is a prefix of the buffers — in lattice order a smaller count would draw only the top rows.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `exponent = 6`
  The p-norm. Below ~4 the shape is round enough that the clear zone bulges past the ends of the line; above ~10 the corners are sharp enough to crease the field visibly, which is the axis-aligned-box failure the superellipse exists to avoid.
- `WHIP_DISC = 0.3`
  Width of the band the interior is compressed into, in normalised units — the whole feel of the effect. Small values whip particles out hard and stack them into a bright outline; past ~0.6 the field bends around from so far away that the text no longer reads as the cause.
- `margin = 0.06`
  Clear ring around the text, in units of container HEIGHT, divided by the aspect ratio for x so the gap is the same number of pixels on all four sides. Adding one uv figure to both halves pads a wide container far more at the ends of the line than above it.
- `pointerRadius / pointerWhip = 0.16 / 0.45`
  The second field, at exponent 2. Softer than the text rect on purpose: the pointer is a passing influence and a hard-edged hole following the cursor competes with the headline it is supposed to frame.
- `smoothing = 0.0008`
  Fraction of the pointer gap still remaining after one second — an ~90ms tail. The pointer hole has a visible edge, unlike a glow, so lag reads as broken rather than as smooth.
- `CELL_JITTER = 0.42`
  Displacement inside a lattice cell, as a fraction of the cell. Zero is a visible grid; past ~0.5 neighbouring cells overlap and the stratification that made the scatter even in the first place is gone.
- `density = 900`
  Particles per megapixel, so the same value reads right in a 320px card and a 2000px hero. Too sparse and the rim is a dotted line rather than a shape.
- `MAX_DPR = 1.5`
  Additive fill is the whole cost and it scales with the square of the ratio. These are soft round dots with no fine detail, so a third sample per axis resolves nothing and costs 78% more fragments.

## API

```ts
function SuperellipseTextAvoidance(props: { children?: ReactNode; density?: number; maxCount?: number; sizeRange?: readonly [number, number]; exponent?: number; margin?: number; whip?: number; pointerRadius?: number; pointerWhip?: number; smoothing?: number; opacity?: number; colorA?: string; colorB?: string; glowColor?: string; background?: string; seed?: number | string; className?: string; textClassName?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `children: ReactNode`
  The headline. Rendered above the field and measured for the avoidance rect.
- `density: number` — default `900`
  Particles per megapixel of container area.
- `maxCount: number` — default `1600`
  Population ceiling, and the size the buffers are allocated at.
- `sizeRange: readonly [number, number]` — default `[1.4, 4.4]`
  Particle size in CSS pixels, biased toward the small end.
- `exponent: number` — default `6`
  Superellipse exponent. 2 is a circle, 6 a squircle, high values a box.
- `margin: number` — default `0.06`
  Clear ring around the text, in units of container height.
- `whip: number` — default `0.3`
  Width of the band the interior is compressed into.
- `pointerRadius: number` — default `0.16`
  Pointer avoidance radius in container-height units. 0 disables it.
- `pointerWhip: number` — default `0.45`
  Whip band for the pointer disc.
- `smoothing: number` — default `0.0008`
  Fraction of the pointer gap still remaining after one second.
- `opacity: number` — default `0.92`
  Overall alpha multiplier.
- `colorA: string` — default `'#9ec6ff'`
  First tint. Any value ogl's Color accepts.
- `colorB: string` — default `'#eef2fb'`
  Second tint; each particle mixes between the two.
- `glowColor: string` — default `'#ffd9a0'`
  Tint for displaced particles, which is what makes the shape legible.
- `background: string` — default `'#07080d'`
  Opaque clear colour the additive field is composited onto.
- `seed: number | string` — default `'superellipse-text-avoidance'`
  Seeds the lattice jitter, sizes, phases and tints.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the root container via `cn`.
- `textClassName: string`
  Merged onto the measured text layer.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
/** Floor on the population. Below this the field reads as a few stray specks. */
const MIN_COUNT = 260;
/**
 * Width of the band interior particles are compressed into, in normalised
 * superellipse units. The catalogue's WHIP_DISC. Small values throw particles
 * out hard and stack them on the outline; large ones bend the field around from
 * a distance and the text stops looking like the cause.
 */
const WHIP_DISC = 0.3;
/** Fraction of the presence gap left after a second. ~200ms in and out. */
const PRESENCE_SMOOTHING = 0.007;
/** Size distribution exponent. Above 1 crowds the population into small sizes. */
const SIZE_BIAS = 1.7;
/** Fill scales with dpr squared, and these are soft dots with no fine detail. */
const MAX_DPR = 1.5;
/** Lattice bounds. Wider than 0..1 so drift never bares the edges. */
const HOME_MIN = -0.05;
const HOME_MAX = 1.05;
/** Jitter as a fraction of a lattice cell. Past ~0.5 cells overlap and clump. */
const CELL_JITTER = 0.42;
/** The reduced-motion still: one frame with the pointer parked off to one side. */
const STILL_ELAPSED = 4.2;
const STILL_POINTER: readonly [number, number] = [0.3, 0.34];

export function SuperellipseTextAvoidance({
  children,
  density = 900,
  maxCount = 1600,
  sizeRange = [1.4, 4.4],
  exponent = 6,
  margin = 0.06,
  whip = WHIP_DISC,
  pointerRadius = 0.16,
  pointerWhip = 0.45,
  smoothing = 0.0008,
  opacity = 0.92,
  colorA = '#9ec6ff',
  colorB = '#eef2fb',
  glowColor = '#ffd9a0',
  background = '#07080d',
  seed = 'superellipse-text-avoidance',
  className,
  textClassName,
}: SuperellipseTextAvoidanceProps) {
  const host = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const text = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const stage = useRef<Stage | null>(null);
  const [unsupported, setUnsupported] = useState(false);

  const { width, height } = useResizeObserver(host);
  const textSize = useResizeObserver(text);
  const size = useRef({ width, height });
  size.current = { width, height };

  const reduced = useReducedMotion();
  const reducedRef = useRef(reduced);
  reducedRef.current = reduced;
  const visible = useVisibility();
  const { inView } = useInView(host, { rootMargin: '10%' });
  const ready = width > 1 && height > 1;

  const [minSize = 1.4, maxSize = 4.4] = sizeRange;

  /* Raw pointer target in field space, or null until a real move — which is not
     the same as a pointer resting at the bottom-left corner. */
  const target = useRef<{ x: number; y: number } | null>(null);
  const inside = useRef(false);
  const follow = useRef({ x: 0.5, y: 0.5 });
  const presence = useRef(0);

  /* Live numbers the loop reads. Changing one must not rebuild the renderer:
     Chromium drops the OLDEST WebGL context past roughly 16 per process, so a
     rebuild per prop change can blank an unrelated canvas on the same page. */
  const live = useRef({ exponent, margin, whip, pointerRadius, pointerWhip, smoothing, opacity });
  live.current = { exponent, margin, whip, pointerRadius, pointerWhip, smoothing, opacity };

  /**
   * Reads the text box out of the DOM and writes it into `uRect` as uv centre
   * plus padded half-extents. No React state: a measurement that re-renders is
   * a measurement that can re-measure itself in a loop.
   */
  const measure = () => {
    const s = stage.current;
    const hostEl = host.current;
    const textEl = text.current;
    if (!s || !hostEl || !textEl) return;

    const hostBox = hostEl.getBoundingClientRect();
    if (hostBox.width < 1 || hostBox.height < 1) return;
    const textBox = textEl.getBoundingClientRect();

    if (textBox.width < 1 || textBox.height < 1) {
      // No children, or the text has not laid out yet. Presence 0 rather than a
      // zero-size rect, which would be a singularity at the centre of the field.
      s.uniforms.uRectPresence.value = 0;
      return;
    }

    const aspect = hostBox.width / hostBox.height;
    /* The margin is specified in HEIGHT units and divided by the aspect ratio
       for x, so the clear ring is the same number of pixels on all four sides.
       Adding the same uv figure to both halves pads a wide container far more
       at the ends of the line than above and below it. */
    const padX = live.current.margin / Math.max(aspect, 0.0001);
    const padY = live.current.margin;

    s.uniforms.uRect.value[0] = (textBox.left - hostBox.left + textBox.width * 0.5) / hostBox.width;
    // Flipped: field y is up, client y is down.
    s.uniforms.uRect.value[1] =
      1 - (textBox.top - hostBox.top + textBox.height * 0.5) / hostBox.height;
    s.uniforms.uRect.value[2] = textBox.width * 0.5 / hostBox.width + padX;
    s.uniforms.uRect.value[3] = textBox.height * 0.5 / hostBox.height + padY;
    s.uniforms.uRectPresence.value = 1;

    // The live loop picks this up next frame; a paused one has to be told.
    if (reducedRef.current) s.draw(STILL_ELAPSED);
  };

  useEffect(() => {
    const el = host.current;
    if (!el || !ready) return;

    if (!hasWebGL()) {
      setUnsupported(true);
      return;
    }

    /* ogl creates its own canvas, and it is appended and removed per effect
       run. Reusing one React-owned canvas breaks under StrictMode: the first
       cleanup force-loses the context, and `getContext` on that element
       afterwards hands back the dead one rather than a fresh context — the
       panel is then permanently blank in development and fine in production. */
    const renderer = new Renderer({
      dpr: pixelRatio(MAX_DPR),
      // Opaque: the pass is additive, and additive onto a transparent canvas
      // would have to brighten the page behind it, which the GPU cannot see.
      alpha: false,
      // Nothing occludes anything, so a depth buffer is memory plus a clear.
      depth: false,
      antialias: false,
      powerPreference: 'low-power',
    });

    const gl = renderer.gl;
    const canvas = gl.canvas;

    const bg = new Color(background);
    gl.clearColor(bg.r, bg.g, bg.b, 1);

    const quad = new Float32Array([-0.5, -0.5, 0.5, -0.5, 0.5, 0.5, -0.5, 0.5]);
    const index = new Uint16Array([0, 1, 2, 0, 2, 3]);

    const total = Math.max(MIN_COUNT, Math.round(maxCount));
    const homes = new Float32Array(total * 2);
    const params = new Float32Array(total * 4);
    const seeds = new Float32Array(total * 4);

    const rng = createRng(seed);

    /* A STRATIFIED scatter, not `rng()` twice. Uniform random has clumps and
       voids at this population, and once the avoidance opens a real hole those
       accidental voids read as more holes — the shape of the field stops being
       legible. A jittered lattice is even everywhere and still looks organic.
       Cells are then SHUFFLED, because the instanced count is a prefix of these
       buffers: in lattice order a smaller count would draw the top rows only. */
    const aspect = Math.max(size.current.width, 1) / Math.max(size.current.height, 1);
    const cols = Math.max(2, Math.round(Math.sqrt(total * aspect)));
    const rows = Math.max(2, Math.ceil(total / cols));
    const cells: Array<[number, number]> = [];
    for (let r = 0; r < rows; r += 1) {
      for (let c = 0; c < cols; c += 1) {
        cells.push([(c + 0.5) / cols, (r + 0.5) / rows]);
      }
    }
    shuffle(rng, cells);

    const spanX = HOME_MAX - HOME_MIN;
    const spanY = HOME_MAX - HOME_MIN;

    for (let i = 0; i < total; i += 1) {
      const cell = cells[i % cells.length] ?? [0.5, 0.5];
      const [cellX = 0.5, cellY = 0.5] = cell;
      homes[i * 2] = HOME_MIN + (cellX + randRange(rng, -CELL_JITTER, CELL_JITTER) / cols) * spanX;
      homes[i * 2 + 1] =
        HOME_MIN + (cellY + randRange(rng, -CELL_JITTER, CELL_JITTER) / rows) * spanY;

      // Biased small: a linear distribution puts a quarter of the population in
      // the largest quarter of the range and the field reads as gravel.
      const sizeT = Math.pow(rng(), SIZE_BIAS);
      params[i * 4] = Math.max(0.5, minSize) + Math.max(maxSize - minSize, 0.25) * sizeT;
      // Drift radius and rate. Small, because this field is a texture the text
      // sits in — a fast one competes with the headline for attention.
      params[i * 4 + 1] = randRange(rng, 0.002, 0.014);
      params[i * 4 + 2] = (rng() < 0.5 ? -1 : 1) * randRange(rng, 0.08, 0.32);
      // Bigger particles are dimmer, so total light stays roughly constant.
      params[i * 4 + 3] = 0.32 + 0.5 * (1 - sizeT);

      seeds[i * 4] = rng() * Math.PI * 2;
      seeds[i * 4 + 1] = randRange(rng, 0.3, 1);
      seeds[i * 4 + 2] = rng();
      seeds[i * 4 + 3] = 0;
    }

    const geometry = new Geometry(gl, {
      index: { data: index },
      position: { size: 2, data: quad },
      aHome: { size: 2, data: homes, instanced: 1 },
      aParams: { size: 4, data: params, instanced: 1 },
      aSeed: { size: 4, data: seeds, instanced: 1 },
    });

    const uniforms: Uniforms = {
      uResolution: { value: [1, 1] },
      uPixelRatio: { value: renderer.dpr },
      uElapsed: { value: 0 },
      uRect: { value: [0.5, 0.5, 0.001, 0.001] },
      uRectPresence: { value: 0 },
      uExponent: { value: clamp(exponent, 2, 16) },
      uWhip: { value: Math.max(whip, 0.02) },
      uPointer: { value: [0.5, 0.5] },
      uPointerPresence: { value: 0 },
      uPointerRadius: { value: Math.max(pointerRadius, 0) },
      uPointerWhip: { value: Math.max(pointerWhip, 0.02) },
      uColorA: { value: new Color(colorA) },
      uColorB: { value: new Color(colorB) },
      uGlowColor: { value: new Color(glowColor) },
      uOpacity: { value: opacity },
    };

    const program = new Program(gl, {
      vertex: SUPERELLIPSE_TEXT_AVOIDANCE_VERT,
      fragment: SUPERELLIPSE_TEXT_AVOIDANCE_FRAG,
      uniforms,
      transparent: true,
      depthTest: false,
      depthWrite: false,
      // ogl culls BACK faces by default and the quad's winding is not
      // guaranteed to face the way the driver expects. A culled particle is not
      // dim — it is absent.
      cullFace: false,
    });
    // Additive, overriding the source-over that `transparent: true` selected.
    // Order independent, so a thousand overlapping instances need no sort.
    program.setBlendFunc(gl.ONE, gl.ONE);

    const mesh = new Mesh(gl, { geometry, program });

    el.insertBefore(canvas, el.firstChild);
    canvas.style.display = 'block';

    /* Listeners on the CANVAS, not the window. A document-level handler
       outlives the renderer it was written for, and the rect it measures is not
       the rect being drawn into — after a scroll the hole sits at an offset
       from the cursor. Passive, because nothing here calls preventDefault and a
       non-passive move handler makes the compositor wait for JS on every event. */
    const onMove = (event: PointerEvent) => {
      const rect = canvas.getBoundingClientRect();
      if (rect.width === 0 || rect.height === 0) return;
      target.current = {
        x: (event.clientX - rect.left) / rect.width,
        y: 1 - (event.clientY - rect.top) / rect.height,
      };
      inside.current = true;
    };
    const onLeave = () => {
      // Position is left where it is. Tweening it back to the centre drags a
      // visible furrow across the field on the way out.
      inside.current = false;
    };

    canvas.addEventListener('pointermove', onMove, { passive: true });
    canvas.addEventListener('pointerleave', onLeave, { passive: true });
    canvas.addEventListener('pointercancel', onLeave, { passive: true });

    const resize = (w: number, h: number) => {
      renderer.setSize(w, h);
      // `setSize` writes literal px into the canvas's inline style, which wins
      // over any class. Re-asserting percentages keeps it fluid between resize
      // notifications.
      canvas.style.width = '100%';
      canvas.style.height = '100%';

      uniforms.uResolution.value = [gl.drawingBufferWidth, gl.drawingBufferHeight];
      uniforms.uPixelRatio.value = renderer.dpr;

      // Population from area, not a fixed number: the same density reads right
      // in a 320px card and a 2000px hero. The buffers already hold `total`
      // particles in shuffled order, so a prefix of them is still spatially
      // even — no rebuild, no reallocation, no new GPU memory.
      const megapixels = (w * h) / 1_000_000;
      const count = clamp(Math.round(megapixels * density), MIN_COUNT, total);
      geometry.setInstancedCount(count);
    };

    const draw = (elapsed: number) => {
      uniforms.uElapsed.value = elapsed;
      renderer.render({ scene: mesh });
    };

    resize(size.current.width, size.current.height);
    stage.current = { renderer, geometry, program, mesh, uniforms, resize, draw };
    measure();
    draw(0);

    /* A webfont swap changes the text box after the first measurement, and
       nothing about a font swap resizes the element's border box on every
       engine — so the ResizeObserver alone is not enough. */
    let cancelled = false;
    if (typeof document !== 'undefined' && 'fonts' in document) {
      void document.fonts.ready.then(() => {
        if (!cancelled) measure();
      });
    }

    return () => {
      cancelled = true;
      stage.current = null;
      canvas.removeEventListener('pointermove', onMove);
      canvas.removeEventListener('pointerleave', onLeave);
      canvas.removeEventListener('pointercancel', onLeave);
      // ogl has no `dispose()`: `remove()` on the geometry deletes its VAOs and
      // every buffer, `remove()` on the program deletes the shaders and the
      // program, and only then is the context worth handing back. Dropping the
      // context is the part that matters — the per-process budget is about
      // sixteen, and exceeding it kills someone else's oldest context.
      geometry.remove();
      program.remove();
      loseContext(gl);
      canvas.width = 0;
      canvas.height = 0;
      canvas.remove();
    };
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, [ready, density, maxCount, minSize, maxSize, seed]);

  // Colours go into the live uniforms rather than being effect deps, so
  // recolouring never costs a context.
  useEffect(() => {
    const s = stage.current;
    if (!s) return;
    s.uniforms.uColorA.value.set(colorA);
    s.uniforms.uColorB.value.set(colorB);
    s.uniforms.uGlowColor.value.set(glowColor);
    const bg = new Color(background);
    s.renderer.gl.clearColor(bg.r, bg.g, bg.b, 1);
  }, [colorA, colorB, glowColor, background]);

  // Resize is its own effect: a reflow costs a `setSize`, an instanced-count
  // change and a re-measure, never a buffer rebuild.
  useEffect(() => {
    stage.current?.resize(width, height);
    measure();
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, [width, height]);

  // The text box changes on its own too — wrapping to a new line, a font swap,
  // or different children entirely.
  useEffect(() => {
    measure();
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, [textSize.width, textSize.height, margin, children]);

  useRaf(
    (dt, elapsed) => {
      const s = stage.current;
      if (!s) return;
      const cfg = live.current;

      const aim = target.current;
      if (aim) {
        follow.current.x = damp(follow.current.x, aim.x, cfg.smoothing, dt);
        follow.current.y = damp(follow.current.y, aim.y, cfg.smoothing, dt);
      }
      presence.current = damp(
        presence.current,
        inside.current && aim !== null ? 1 : 0,
        PRESENCE_SMOOTHING,
        dt,
      );

      const u = s.uniforms;
      // Mutated in place. Assigning a fresh tuple allocates an array a frame and
      // defeats ogl's redundant-uniform cache, which compares by length first
      // and then element by element against the array it kept.
      u.uPointer.value[0] = follow.current.x;
      u.uPointer.value[1] = follow.current.y;
      u.uPointerPresence.value = presence.current;
      u.uPointerRadius.value = Math.max(cfg.pointerRadius, 0);
      u.uPointerWhip.value = Math.max(cfg.pointerWhip, 0.02);
      u.uExponent.value = clamp(cfg.exponent, 2, 16);
      u.uWhip.value = Math.max(cfg.whip, 0.02);
      u.uOpacity.value = cfg.opacity;

      s.draw(elapsed);
    },
    ready && inView && visible && !reduced && !unsupported,
  );

  /* Reduced motion is a composed still, not an empty box: one frame with the
     text rect fully avoided and the pointer parked off to one side, so the
     shape of the field is exactly what a moving version would show. The
     listeners stay attached and their target is never consumed. */
  useEffect(() => {
    const s = stage.current;
    if (!s || !reduced || !ready) return;
    const [px = 0.3, py = 0.34] = STILL_POINTER;
    s.uniforms.uPointer.value[0] = px;
    s.uniforms.uPointer.value[1] = py;
    s.uniforms.uPointerPresence.value = 1;
    s.draw(STILL_ELAPSED);
  }, [reduced, ready, width, height]);
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** Removes the three pointer listeners from the canvas, cancels the pending `document.fonts.ready` callback with a flag, nulls the stage ref so an in-flight frame cannot touch a dead renderer, then `geometry.remove()` (deletes the VAOs and every buffer), `program.remove()` (deletes the shaders and the program), `loseContext(gl)`, zeroes the canvas dimensions and removes it from the DOM. ogl has no `dispose()`, and dropping the context is the part that matters — the per-process budget is about sixteen, and exceeding it kills the oldest, which belongs to someone else.

**Reduced motion.** The loop never starts. One frame is drawn with the text rect fully avoided and the pointer parked off to one side at full presence, so the still shows exactly the shape a moving version produces — the drift is the only thing lost. Re-measuring after a font swap redraws that single frame rather than starting a loop. The listeners stay attached but their target is never consumed.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Using `normalize()` for the push direction. It is NaN at the origin, and NaN in `gl_Position` discards the entire primitive — so the bug looks like missing particles, not like a maths error.
- `pow()` with a negative base or a zero base. Both are undefined in GLSL, both are reached on the axes of a symmetric field, and the result is driver-dependent: fine on the machine it was written on, black on someone else's.
- Clamping interior particles onto the shell instead of remapping their radius. Every particle inside lands exactly on the outline, so the shape is one dense curve with a dead interior behind it — visibly a stencil rather than a field flowing around something.
- Hard-coding the text rect, or deriving it from a character count. It is wrong the moment a webfont swaps, the line rewraps, or the container narrows, and the hole drifts off the words while still looking deliberate.
- Relying on the ResizeObserver alone for the text box. A font swap does not necessarily change the element's border box on every engine, so the measurement has to be repeated after `document.fonts.ready` as well.
- Aspect-correcting the text rect. It was measured in element space; correcting it clears a region visibly narrower than the headline on a wide container, which is worse than not avoiding at all.
- Forgetting to aspect-correct the POINTER disc. Exactly the opposite case — a screen-space shape left uncorrected is an obvious ellipse on anything but a square container.
- Writing pointer events straight into `uPointer`. A high-rate trackpad delivers a staircase, and after a stalled frame it is a jump that drags the hole across the field in one step. The listener records a target; the loop damps toward it.
- Damping with a per-frame constant (`x += (t - x) * 0.1`) instead of `damp(..., dt)`. The follow is visibly tighter at 120Hz than at 60Hz, so the feel is tuned to whichever display it was authored on.
- Scattering with `rng()` twice. The clumps and voids of a uniform random field are indistinguishable from more avoidance holes once the real one exists. A jittered lattice, shuffled so the instanced-count prefix is still spatially even, costs the same.
- Leaving ogl's default BACK-face culling on. The quad winding is not guaranteed to face the way the driver expects, and a culled particle is not dim — it is absent, so the field renders empty on some machines and fine on others.
- Owning the canvas in React while calling `loseContext()` on cleanup. Under `reactStrictMode` the effect runs twice and the second `getContext` on that element returns the dead context: blank in development, fine in production.
- Letting the text layer swallow pointer events. It sits above the canvas, so without `pointer-events: none` the pointer hole disappears whenever the cursor crosses the headline — precisely where the effect is most visible.
- Re-measuring through React state. A measurement that triggers a render can trigger another measurement; the rect is written straight into the uniform instead.

## Notes

- `children` is the headline and is rendered as real DOM above the field, so it is selectable, searchable and styled with ordinary classes. The component only reads its box.
- The text layer is `pointer-events: none` so the canvas underneath keeps receiving moves. Anything interactive belongs outside it.
- The same `avoid()` function serves both fields; the pointer is just exponent 2 with a wider whip. Adding a third avoided region is one more call, not one more code path.
- Blending is additive with an opaque clear colour, so a thousand overlapping instances need no depth sort and the whole field is one draw call. The fragment output is premultiplied because the destination is only ever added to.
- Population is derived from container area and selected with `setInstancedCount` out of buffers allocated once at `maxCount`, so a resize changes the count without touching GPU memory.
- The scatter runs on `createRng(seed)`, never `Math.random()`, so the field is identical on every load and a visual regression is a real regression.

## Definition of done

The headline sits in a clear zone whose shape is a squircle, not a circle and not a rectangle: the gap above and below the line is the same as the gap at its ends, and the corners are rounded without being round. A brighter rim traces that shape. Resize the container until the headline rewraps to two lines — the clear zone re-fits within a frame, with no visible sweep from the old rect. Move the pointer in and a second, softer hole follows it with a short even lag that is identical on a 60Hz and a 120Hz display; the hole stays circular on a wide container and does not disappear when the pointer crosses the headline. No particle sits inside the clear zone and none pile into a single dense outline. Reload twice: the field is identical. With reduced motion the panel is one composed still with the same shape.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.

# Build: Area-Weighted Surface Particles

Turns any object — one primitive or a whole loaded model — into a particle shell whose density is uniform over the surface rather than over the mesh list. One cumulative distribution is built over the world-space area of every triangle in the object and sampled by binary search, so a face a thousand times larger than its neighbour is picked a thousand times more often. The shell then assembles bottom-up on a per-particle window, breathes along its own sampled normals, and is ringed by orbit lines whose radii are measured from the cloud instead of hard-coded.

Build this as a React component in my project. Match my existing conventions —
file layout, styling system, and naming — rather than the ones implied below.
Everything after this line is specification, not code to copy verbatim.

## What it does

Any mesh becomes a particle shell of even density, assembling bottom-up, with orbit rings measured off the sampled silhouette.

- Category: webgl
- Runtime cost: webgl
- Dependencies: three@^0.185.1

## How it works

1. Every mesh under the source object is traversed and each triangle is read in WORLD space via `matrixWorld`. `n = (b - a) × (c - a)` gives area as `|n| / 2` and the face normal as `n / |n|` in one operation; the running area total is written into a `Float64Array` cumulative table, one entry per triangle.
2. To place a particle, `rng() * totalArea` is looked up in that table by binary search. This is inverse-transform sampling over area, which is where per-mesh weighting comes from for free — the alternative, `count / meshCount` points per mesh, gives a dense speckle on the small parts and a sparse haze on the large ones, and no tuning fixes it because the error is structural.
3. The point inside the chosen triangle uses barycentric coordinates by reflection: draw `u, v` in the unit square and if `u + v > 1` replace them with `1 - u, 1 - v`, folding the far half back across the diagonal. `p = a + (b - a) * u + (c - a) * v` is then exactly uniform over the triangle.
4. The cloud is centred on its bounding-box centre and divided by its farthest sample, so the shell always has bounding-sphere radius 1. Camera distance follows from the frustum rather than from taste: `d = 1 / sin(min(vFovHalf, atan(tan(vFovHalf) * aspect))) * 1.14` fits the sphere in whichever axis is tighter.
5. Assembly order is the particle's own normalised target height, so `form = smoothstep(order * 0.45, order * 0.45 + 0.55, uForm)` builds the shell bottom-up — the object is constructed rather than faded in. `uForm` is damped toward 1 with `damp(form, 1, 0.05, dt)`, so the build takes about the same two seconds at 60 and at 120 Hz.
6. `eff = uScatter * (1 - form)` collapses the pre-assembly cloud into the arrival: each particle is pushed out along `normalize(aRand.xyz - 0.5 + 0.0001)` by `(0.6 + aRand.x * 2.2)` radii plus a slow per-axis sinusoid, and both fade to nothing exactly as that particle's own window closes.
7. Point size is perspective-corrected in the vertex shader: `uSize * jitter * uSizeScale / max(0.1, -mv.z)`, where `uSizeScale` is `pixelRatio * cameraDistance`. That makes `uSize` a literal CSS-pixel diameter for a particle at the centre of the shell, rather than the tuned constant this term usually is.
8. Orbit rings are measured, not authored: the cloud is cut into `ringCount` horizontal bands, the radii `sqrt(x² + z²)` within each band are sorted, and the 92nd percentile times 1.06 is the ring radius. Bands with fewer than 12 samples are skipped. All rings go into one buffer as `LineSegments`, so the set is one draw call.

## Constants — use these values

These are tuned. Each one has a reason; do not round them off or replace them
with values that "look cleaner".

- `count = 9000`
  Particles, one buffer, one draw call. Enough that the silhouette of a torus knot reads as a solid surface at preview size; the cost is fill rather than vertex count, and doubling it doubles the blended pixel area rather than the detail.
- `size / maxSize = 2.4 / 22 CSS px`
  Diameter at the centre of the shell, and the ceiling after 1/z growth. The clamp is not cosmetic: a particle that drifts close to the near plane would otherwise ask for a point size in the thousands, which drivers answer by silently capping — or by dropping the draw call.
- `size jitter = 0.55 + aRand.w * 1.35`
  A 3.4x spread. With every particle the same size the cloud reads as a halftone screen; much wider and the largest sprites stop looking like members of the same population.
- `STAGGER / WINDOW = 0.45 / 0.55`
  They sum to exactly 1.0, so the last particle to start is also the one that finishes as `uForm` reaches 1 — no dead time at either end of the build. Raising STAGGER past ~0.6 leaves the base fully assembled while the top has not begun, which reads as two separate animations.
- `FORM_SMOOTHING = 0.05`
  Fraction of the assembly gap remaining after one second, which with the stagger gives a build of roughly two seconds. This is a `damp` smoothing value, not a per-frame lerp — the per-frame form of the same curve converges twice as fast at 120 Hz.
- `FORM_EPSILON = 0.9995`
  `damp` is asymptotic and never arrives, but the last stagger window needs `uForm` to reach exactly 1.0 or the topmost particles stay a hair short of their target forever. Past this threshold it snaps.
- `puff = 0.02 of the shell radius`
  Breathing amplitude along the sampled normal. At 2% the surface undulates while staying a surface; past roughly 6% the shell loses its silhouette and reads as a cloud that happens to be shaped like the object.
- `scatter = 0.9`
  Pre-assembly spread in shell radii, giving a cloud extending to about 2.6 radii. Small enough that the unformed state is still recognisably centred on the object; much larger and the particles start their travel off-screen, so the build begins with an empty frame.
- `RING_PERCENTILE = 0.92`
  Which measured radius in a band becomes the ring. The maximum is dragged outward by a single stray sample on a spike; the mean sinks inside the silhouette and the ring cuts through the shell.
- `MIN_BAND_SAMPLES / MIN_RING_RADIUS = 12 / 0.08`
  A band with almost nothing in it is a gap in the model, and a ring there would hang in empty air; a measured radius near zero is a dot rather than a ring. Both are skipped, which is why the ring count is a maximum and not a promise.
- `FIT_PADDING = 1.14`
  Slack between the unit sphere and the frustum. It has to cover the breathing, the ring margin and the fact that a sprite is drawn centred on its vertex, so a particle exactly on the silhouette still needs half its own width of room.
- `TILT = 0.2 rad`
  Static tilt applied on a parent group. Without it the measured rings project to straight lines and read as scan lines rather than orbits; much past 0.4 the top band occludes the shell.
- `RING_SEGMENTS = 128`
  Vertices per ring. Roughly where a hairline circle stops showing flats at 600px wide, and cheap enough that four rings are still 1024 line vertices in a single buffer.

## API

```ts
function SurfaceSampledParticles(props: { source?: () => THREE.Object3D | null; count?: number; size?: number; maxSize?: number; spin?: number; puff?: number; scatter?: number; ringCount?: number; ringOpacity?: number; opacity?: number; colorBase?: string; colorTip?: string; ringColor?: string; fov?: number; seed?: number | string; className?: string }): JSX.Element
```

- `source: () => THREE.Object3D | null`
  Builds the object to sample. Measured on the CPU, never added to the scene, disposed once sampling finishes. Held in a ref, so changing it does not itself trigger a rebuild.
- `count: number` — default `9000`
  Particle count. One buffer, one draw call; cost is linear in fill.
- `size: number` — default `2.4`
  Particle diameter in CSS pixels for a particle at the centre of the shell.
- `maxSize: number` — default `22`
  Ceiling in CSS pixels on the perspective-grown size.
- `spin: number` — default `0.16`
  Turntable speed in radians per second.
- `puff: number` — default `0.02`
  Breathing amplitude along the sampled normal, as a fraction of the shell radius.
- `scatter: number` — default `0.9`
  How far the pre-assembly cloud spreads, in shell radii.
- `ringCount: number` — default `4`
  Horizontal bands to measure orbit rings from. Bands that are too empty are skipped, so this is a maximum. 0 disables the rings.
- `ringOpacity: number` — default `0.3`
  Ring opacity once the shell has assembled; it ramps with the build.
- `opacity: number` — default `0.9`
  Overall alpha multiplier applied in the vertex shader.
- `colorBase: string` — default `'#6b7783'`
  Tint at the base of the shell.
- `colorTip: string` — default `'#ffffff'`
  Tint at the top of the shell.
- `ringColor: string` — default `'#8d9aa6'`
  Ring colour.
- `fov: number` — default `32`
  Vertical field of view in degrees. Camera distance and the perspective size term are both derived from it.
- `seed: number | string` — default `'surface-sampled-particles'`
  Seeds the sampling and the per-particle randoms, so the same shell is produced on the server and on every reload.
- `className: string`
  Merged onto the host element via `cn`.

## Reference implementation of the core

This is the part that is hard to get right. Adapt it; do not treat the rest of
the component as fixed.

```tsx
/**
 * Sample `count` points over the total world-space surface area of everything
 * under `root`, then centre and scale the result so its bounding sphere has
 * radius 1.
 */
function sampleSurface(root: THREE.Object3D, count: number, rng: Rng): Shell | null {
  // World matrices, not local ones: a mesh scaled 10x has 100x the area, and
  // sampling in local space would weight it as though it did not.
  root.updateMatrixWorld(true);

  const meshes: THREE.Mesh[] = [];
  root.traverse((obj) => {
    const mesh = obj as THREE.Mesh;
    if (mesh.isMesh && mesh.geometry) meshes.push(mesh);
  });

  let capacity = 0;
  for (const mesh of meshes) {
    const position = mesh.geometry.getAttribute('position');
    if (!position) continue;
    const index = mesh.geometry.getIndex();
    capacity += Math.floor((index ? index.count : position.count) / 3);
  }
  if (capacity === 0) return null;

  const tri = new Float32Array(capacity * 9);
  const triNormal = new Float32Array(capacity * 3);
  // Float64 for the running total. At tens of thousands of triangles a Float32
  // accumulator loses the smallest ones entirely — they land inside the
  // rounding error of the sum and become unreachable by any sample.
  const cumulative = new Float64Array(capacity);

  const a = new THREE.Vector3();
  const b = new THREE.Vector3();
  const c = new THREE.Vector3();
  const ab = new THREE.Vector3();
  const ac = new THREE.Vector3();
  const n = new THREE.Vector3();

  let triCount = 0;
  let total = 0;

  for (const mesh of meshes) {
    const position = mesh.geometry.getAttribute('position');
    if (!position) continue;
    const index = mesh.geometry.getIndex();
    const faces = Math.floor((index ? index.count : position.count) / 3);

    for (let f = 0; f < faces; f += 1) {
      const i0 = index ? index.getX(f * 3) : f * 3;
      const i1 = index ? index.getX(f * 3 + 1) : f * 3 + 1;
      const i2 = index ? index.getX(f * 3 + 2) : f * 3 + 2;

      a.fromBufferAttribute(position, i0).applyMatrix4(mesh.matrixWorld);
      b.fromBufferAttribute(position, i1).applyMatrix4(mesh.matrixWorld);
      c.fromBufferAttribute(position, i2).applyMatrix4(mesh.matrixWorld);

      ab.subVectors(b, a);
      ac.subVectors(c, a);
      n.crossVectors(ab, ac);
      // Half the cross product's magnitude is the triangle's area, and the
      // cross product's direction is its normal — one operation for both.
      const area = n.length() * 0.5;
      // Degenerate triangles are common in generated and exported geometry.
      // Keeping them would put zero-width steps in the distribution and, worse,
      // normalising a zero-length normal yields NaN.
      if (!(area > 0)) continue;
      n.divideScalar(area * 2);

      const t9 = triCount * 9;
      tri[t9] = a.x;
      tri[t9 + 1] = a.y;
      tri[t9 + 2] = a.z;
      tri[t9 + 3] = ab.x;
      tri[t9 + 4] = ab.y;
      tri[t9 + 5] = ab.z;
      tri[t9 + 6] = ac.x;
      tri[t9 + 7] = ac.y;
      tri[t9 + 8] = ac.z;

      const t3 = triCount * 3;
      triNormal[t3] = n.x;
      triNormal[t3 + 1] = n.y;
      triNormal[t3 + 2] = n.z;

      total += area;
      cumulative[triCount] = total;
      triCount += 1;
    }
  }

  if (triCount === 0 || total <= 0) return null;

  const positions = new Float32Array(count * 3);
  const normals = new Float32Array(count * 3);
  const rands = new Float32Array(count * 4);
  const orders = new Float32Array(count);

  let minX = Infinity;
  let minY = Infinity;
  let minZ = Infinity;
  let maxX = -Infinity;
  let maxY = -Infinity;
  let maxZ = -Infinity;

  for (let i = 0; i < count; i += 1) {
    // Inverse-transform sampling: a uniform draw across the cumulative area
    // picks each triangle in proportion to its own area, which is exactly the
    // per-mesh weighting the naive loop gets wrong.
    const t = lowerBound(cumulative, triCount, rng() * total);
    const t9 = t * 9;
    const t3 = t * 3;

    // Uniform barycentric coordinates by reflection: draw a point in the unit
    // square and fold the far half back across the diagonal. Cheaper than the
    // sqrt form and exactly uniform, where using u and v raw would pile
    // samples into one corner of every triangle.
    let u = rng();
    let v = rng();
    if (u + v > 1) {
      u = 1 - u;
      v = 1 - v;
    }

    const px = (tri[t9] ?? 0) + (tri[t9 + 3] ?? 0) * u + (tri[t9 + 6] ?? 0) * v;
    const py = (tri[t9 + 1] ?? 0) + (tri[t9 + 4] ?? 0) * u + (tri[t9 + 7] ?? 0) * v;
    const pz = (tri[t9 + 2] ?? 0) + (tri[t9 + 5] ?? 0) * u + (tri[t9 + 8] ?? 0) * v;

    positions[i * 3] = px;
    positions[i * 3 + 1] = py;
    positions[i * 3 + 2] = pz;

    normals[i * 3] = triNormal[t3] ?? 0;
    normals[i * 3 + 1] = triNormal[t3 + 1] ?? 0;
    normals[i * 3 + 2] = triNormal[t3 + 2] ?? 1;

    rands[i * 4] = rng();
    rands[i * 4 + 1] = rng();
    rands[i * 4 + 2] = rng();
    rands[i * 4 + 3] = rng();

    if (px < minX) minX = px;
    if (py < minY) minY = py;
    if (pz < minZ) minZ = pz;
    if (px > maxX) maxX = px;
    if (py > maxY) maxY = py;
    if (pz > maxZ) maxZ = pz;
  }

  // Fit to a unit bounding sphere around the box centre. Normalising here is
  // what lets `puff`, `scatter` and the camera distance be authored once and
  // stay correct for a source of any scale — including a model in metres.
  const cx = (minX + maxX) * 0.5;
  const cy = (minY + maxY) * 0.5;
  const cz = (minZ + maxZ) * 0.5;

  let maxDist = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < count; i += 1) {
    const dx = (positions[i * 3] ?? 0) - cx;
    const dy = (positions[i * 3 + 1] ?? 0) - cy;
    const dz = (positions[i * 3 + 2] ?? 0) - cz;
    const d = Math.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz);
    if (d > maxDist) maxDist = d;
  }
  const scale = maxDist > 0 ? SHELL_RADIUS / maxDist : 1;

  let shellMinY = Infinity;
  let shellMaxY = -Infinity;
  for (let i = 0; i < count; i += 1) {
    const x = ((positions[i * 3] ?? 0) - cx) * scale;
    const y = ((positions[i * 3 + 1] ?? 0) - cy) * scale;
    const z = ((positions[i * 3 + 2] ?? 0) - cz) * scale;
    positions[i * 3] = x;
    positions[i * 3 + 1] = y;
    positions[i * 3 + 2] = z;
    if (y < shellMinY) shellMinY = y;
    if (y > shellMaxY) shellMaxY = y;
  }

  // Assembly order is the particle's own target height, so the shell builds
  // bottom-up. Deriving order from the destination rather than from the buffer
  // index is what makes the build read as construction instead of as noise
  // resolving.
  const span = Math.max(1e-6, shellMaxY - shellMinY);
  for (let i = 0; i < count; i += 1) {
    orders[i] = ((positions[i * 3 + 1] ?? 0) - shellMinY) / span;
  }

  return { positions, normals, rands, orders, minY: shellMinY, maxY: shellMaxY };
}

/**
 * Measure the cloud's silhouette radius in `bands` horizontal slices. The ring
 * radii come out of the geometry that was actually sampled, so swapping the
 * source does not need a new set of hand-tuned numbers.
 */
function measureRings(shell: Shell, bands: number, count: number): Ring[] {
  if (bands <= 0) return [];
  const span = shell.maxY - shell.minY;
  if (!(span > 0)) return [];

  const rings: Ring[] = [];
  for (let band = 0; band < bands; band += 1) {
    const y0 = shell.minY + (span * band) / bands;
    const y1 = shell.minY + (span * (band + 1)) / bands;

    const radii: number[] = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < count; i += 1) {
      const y = shell.positions[i * 3 + 1] ?? 0;
      if (y < y0 || y >= y1) continue;
      const x = shell.positions[i * 3] ?? 0;
      const z = shell.positions[i * 3 + 2] ?? 0;
      radii.push(Math.sqrt(x * x + z * z));
    }
    if (radii.length < MIN_BAND_SAMPLES) continue;

    radii.sort((p, q) => p - q);
    const at = Math.min(radii.length - 1, Math.floor(RING_PERCENTILE * (radii.length - 1)));
    const radius = (radii[at] ?? 0) * RING_MARGIN;
    if (radius < MIN_RING_RADIUS) continue;

    rings.push({ y: (y0 + y1) * 0.5, radius });
  }
  return rings;
}

/** All rings in one buffer, so the whole set is one draw call. */
function buildRingGeometry(rings: Ring[]): THREE.BufferGeometry {
  const vertices = new Float32Array(rings.length * RING_SEGMENTS * 2 * 3);
  let at = 0;
  for (const ring of rings) {
    for (let s = 0; s < RING_SEGMENTS; s += 1) {
      const a0 = (s / RING_SEGMENTS) * Math.PI * 2;
      const a1 = ((s + 1) / RING_SEGMENTS) * Math.PI * 2;
      vertices[at] = Math.cos(a0) * ring.radius;
      vertices[at + 1] = ring.y;
      vertices[at + 2] = Math.sin(a0) * ring.radius;
      vertices[at + 3] = Math.cos(a1) * ring.radius;
      vertices[at + 4] = ring.y;
      vertices[at + 5] = Math.sin(a1) * ring.radius;
      at += 6;
    }
  }
  const geometry = new THREE.BufferGeometry();
  geometry.setAttribute('position', new THREE.BufferAttribute(vertices, 3));
  return geometry;
}

export function SurfaceSampledParticles({
  source,
  count = 9000,
  size = 2.4,
  maxSize = 22,
  spin = 0.16,
  puff = 0.02,
  scatter = 0.9,
  ringCount = 4,
  ringOpacity = 0.3,
  opacity = 0.9,
  colorBase = '#6b7783',
  colorTip = '#ffffff',
  ringColor = '#8d9aa6',
  fov = 32,
  seed = 'surface-sampled-particles',
  className,
}: SurfaceSampledParticlesProps) {
  const host = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const stage = useRef<Stage | null>(null);
  const [unsupported, setUnsupported] = useState(false);

  const sourceRef = useRef(source);
  sourceRef.current = source;

  const { width, height } = useResizeObserver(host);
  const box = useRef({ width, height });
  box.current = { width, height };

  const reduced = useReducedMotion();
  const visible = useVisibility();
  const { inView } = useInView(host, { rootMargin: '10%' });
  const ready = width > 0 && height > 0;

  useEffect(() => {
    const el = host.current;
    if (!el || !ready) return;

    if (!hasWebGL()) {
      setUnsupported(true);
      return;
    }

    // The source object exists only to be measured. It is never added to the
    // scene, so nothing about it is ever uploaded to the GPU, and it is
    // disposed the moment sampling is done.
    const specimen = sourceRef.current?.() ?? buildDefaultSpecimen();
    const rng = createRng(seed);
    const total = Math.max(1, Math.round(count));
    const shell = sampleSurface(specimen, total, rng);
    disposeObject(specimen);
    if (!shell) {
      setUnsupported(true);
      return;
    }

    const renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer({ antialias: false, alpha: true });
    renderer.setPixelRatio(pixelRatio());
    renderer.setClearAlpha(0);
    const dpr = renderer.getPixelRatio();

    const scene = new THREE.Scene();
    const camera = new THREE.PerspectiveCamera(fov, 1, 0.1, 100);

    // Tilt outside, turntable inside: composing both on one Euler makes the
    // spin axis tilt with the object, which wobbles instead of turning.
    const tilt = new THREE.Group();
    tilt.rotation.x = TILT;
    const turntable = new THREE.Group();
    tilt.add(turntable);
    scene.add(tilt);

    const geometry = new THREE.BufferGeometry();
    geometry.setAttribute('position', new THREE.BufferAttribute(shell.positions, 3));
    geometry.setAttribute('aNormal', new THREE.BufferAttribute(shell.normals, 3));
    geometry.setAttribute('aRand', new THREE.BufferAttribute(shell.rands, 4));
    geometry.setAttribute('aOrder', new THREE.BufferAttribute(shell.orders, 1));

    const uniforms: Uniforms = {
      uElapsed: { value: 0 },
      uForm: { value: 0 },
      uScatter: { value: scatter },
      uPuff: { value: puff },
      uSize: { value: size },
      uMaxSize: { value: maxSize * dpr },
      uSizeScale: { value: dpr },
      uOpacity: { value: opacity },
      uColorBase: { value: new THREE.Color(colorBase) },
      uColorTip: { value: new THREE.Color(colorTip) },
    };

    const material = new THREE.ShaderMaterial({
      vertexShader: SURFACE_SAMPLED_PARTICLES_VERT,
      fragmentShader: SURFACE_SAMPLED_PARTICLES_FRAG,
      uniforms,
      transparent: true,
      // No depth at all. Sorting nine thousand points per frame on the CPU is
      // not affordable, and it is not needed: the samples are in random buffer
      // order, so an unsorted alpha blend averages out into even density
      // rather than into visible layers.
      depthTest: false,
      depthWrite: false,
      blending: THREE.NormalBlending,
    });

    const points = new THREE.Points(geometry, material);
    // Displacement happens in the shader, where the frustum culler cannot see
    // it. The bounding sphere three computes from the rest positions is right
    // for the assembled shell and much too small for the scattered one.
    points.frustumCulled = false;
    turntable.add(points);

    const rings = measureRings(shell, Math.max(0, Math.round(ringCount)), total);
    let ringMaterial: THREE.LineBasicMaterial | null = null;
    if (rings.length > 0) {
      ringMaterial = new THREE.LineBasicMaterial({
        color: new THREE.Color(ringColor),
        transparent: true,
        opacity: 0,
        depthTest: false,
        depthWrite: false,
      });
      const ringLines = new THREE.LineSegments(buildRingGeometry(rings), ringMaterial);
      ringLines.frustumCulled = false;
      turntable.add(ringLines);
    }

    el.appendChild(renderer.domElement);
    renderer.domElement.style.display = 'block';
    renderer.domElement.style.width = '100%';
    renderer.domElement.style.height = '100%';

    let form = 0;
    let angle = 0;

    const resize = (w: number, h: number) => {
      if (w <= 0 || h <= 0) return;
      renderer.setSize(w, h, false);
      camera.aspect = w / h;

      // Fit the unit sphere in BOTH axes. Vertical fov alone leaves a tall
      // preview cropping the shell; the horizontal half-angle is the binding
      // constraint whenever the container is narrower than it is tall.
      const vHalf = (camera.fov * Math.PI) / 360;
      const hHalf = Math.atan(Math.tan(vHalf) * camera.aspect);
      const distance = (SHELL_RADIUS / Math.sin(Math.min(vHalf, hHalf))) * FIT_PADDING;
      camera.position.set(0, 0, distance);
      camera.far = distance + SHELL_RADIUS * 8;
      camera.updateProjectionMatrix();

      // Camera distance is half of the perspective size term, so it has to be
      // republished whenever the fit changes — otherwise particles keep the
      // pixel size of the previous layout.
      uniforms.uSizeScale.value = renderer.getPixelRatio() * distance;
      uniforms.uMaxSize.value = maxSize * renderer.getPixelRatio();
    };

    const render = () => {
      uniforms.uForm.value = form;
      turntable.rotation.y = angle;
      if (ringMaterial) ringMaterial.opacity = ringOpacity * form;
      renderer.render(scene, camera);
    };

    const step = (dt: number, elapsed: number) => {
      // Frame-rate independent: a per-frame constant would build the shell
      // twice as fast on a 120 Hz display.
      form = form >= FORM_EPSILON ? 1 : damp(form, 1, FORM_SMOOTHING, dt);
      angle += dt * spin;
      uniforms.uElapsed.value = elapsed;
      render();
    };

    const still = () => {
      form = 1;
      angle = STATIC_ANGLE;
      uniforms.uElapsed.value = STATIC_ELAPSED;
      render();
    };

    resize(box.current.width, box.current.height);
    stage.current = { resize, step, still };
    render();

    return () => {
      stage.current = null;
      disposeObject(scene);
      material.dispose();
      ringMaterial?.dispose();
      disposeRenderer(renderer);
      renderer.domElement.remove();
    };
  }, [
    ready,
    count,
    size,
    maxSize,
    spin,
    puff,
    scatter,
    ringCount,
    ringOpacity,
    opacity,
    colorBase,
    colorTip,
    ringColor,
    fov,
    seed,
  ]);

  // Resize is its own effect: a container reflow costs a `setSize` and a
  // camera refit, never a re-sample of the surface.
  useEffect(() => {
    stage.current?.resize(width, height);
    if (reduced) stage.current?.still();
  }, [width, height, reduced]);

  useRaf(
    (dt, elapsed) => stage.current?.step(dt, elapsed),
    ready && inView && visible && !reduced && !unsupported,
  );
```

## Requirements

These are not optional. A version of this component that skips any of them is
not finished.

**Cleanup.** The source object is disposed immediately after sampling, before the renderer even exists. On unmount the stage ref is nulled so an in-flight frame cannot draw into a dying context, `disposeObject(scene)` disposes the point geometry, the ring geometry and their materials, the point material and the ring material are disposed explicitly as well, then `disposeRenderer` performs `dispose()` + `forceContextLoss()` + a zeroed drawing buffer — `dispose()` alone leaves the context alive — and the canvas node is removed. `useRaf`, `useInView`, `useVisibility` and `useResizeObserver` release their own subscriptions.

**Reduced motion.** No rAF subscription is opened and one still frame is drawn with `uForm` forced to 1 and the turntable at 0.6 rad — a three-quarter view of the fully assembled shell with its rings at full opacity, not the unformed cloud. The shell, the density, the depth cue from perspective point sizing and the measured rings are all present; the assembly, the breathing and the rotation are what stop. A resize redraws the same still.

**Frame-rate independence.** Any smoothing must be a function of delta time.
`x += (target - x) * 0.1` converges twice as fast at 120 Hz as at 60 Hz; use
`x = target + (x - target) * Math.pow(smoothing, dt)` instead, where
`smoothing` is the fraction of the gap remaining after one second.

**Strict mode.** Assume effects run twice in development. Setup must be
idempotent and teardown must fully undo it.

## Known pitfalls — avoid these specifically

- Sampling a fixed number of points per mesh. It is the obvious loop and it is wrong: density then tracks the mesh list rather than the surface, so a model whose parts differ in size gets a dense speckle on the small ones and a haze on the large ones. One cumulative table over all triangles of all meshes is the fix, and it is no more code.
- Building the area table in local space. A mesh scaled 10x has 100x the surface area; weighting by untransformed triangles gives that part a hundredth of the density it should have, and the bug only shows on models that use node transforms.
- Accumulating the running area total in a `Float32Array`. At tens of thousands of triangles the smallest ones land inside the rounding error of the sum, their cumulative entries stop increasing, and they become unreachable by any sample — whole thin features silently receive no particles.
- Keeping degenerate triangles. Exported and generated geometry is full of zero-area faces; they contribute zero-width steps to the distribution and, worse, normalising a zero-length cross product yields NaN. One NaN vertex position takes visible neighbours with it on some drivers.
- Using `u` and `v` raw as barycentric weights. Points then pile into one corner of every triangle, and at high triangle counts the cloud acquires a visible directional grain along the tessellation. Reflecting the far half of the unit square across the diagonal costs one comparison and is exactly uniform.
- Leaving `frustumCulled` on. Every displacement happens in the vertex shader, so the bounding sphere three computes from the rest positions is right for the assembled shell and far too small for the scattered one — the whole cloud blinks out during the part of the animation where it is largest.
- Making `gl_PointSize` constant. Point size does not fall off with distance on its own, so a 3D cloud with a fixed size has no depth at all — it looks like a flat stencil of the object. Dividing by view-space depth is the entire perspective cue, and `max(0.1, -mv.z)` is a required guard, not a nicety: a particle crossing the near plane otherwise asks for an infinite size and some drivers drop the draw.
- Caching the perspective size term at construction. Camera distance is derived from the container aspect ratio, so it changes on every reflow; a stale `uSizeScale` leaves particles at the pixel size of the previous layout.
- Depth-testing a translucent point cloud. With `depthWrite` on, nine thousand sprites occlude each other in buffer order and the cloud tears into hard layers; sorting them per frame on the CPU is unaffordable. Because the samples are already in random order, no depth and an unsorted blend average out into even density.
- Hard-coding ring radii for the model you happen to be sampling. They stop matching the moment the source changes, and nothing in the code says why the numbers were what they were. Measuring a percentile of the cloud's own radius per band is the same three lines and survives a new source.
- Adding the source object to the scene so it can be sampled. It never needs to be rendered — it is a CPU-side measuring stick. Leaving it in the graph uploads every one of its triangles to the GPU and draws a solid mesh through the middle of the particles.
- Making the `source` callback an effect dependency. An inline arrow changes identity on every parent render, so the entire surface is re-sampled — tens of thousands of triangles and a full buffer upload — on any unrelated state change upstream. It is held in a ref instead.

## Notes

- The technique is the same one used to scatter particles over a loaded GLB; the built-in specimen exists so the component ships with no asset. It is four primitives with deliberately mismatched areas — a torus knot, a small icosahedral finial, an open cylinder stem and a lathed base — which is precisely the case area weighting exists to handle.
- Pass `source` to sample something else: return the `scene` of a loaded model, or any procedural `Object3D`. It is measured, normalised to a unit bounding sphere and then disposed, so a source authored in metres and one authored in unit space both frame identically.
- Sampling costs one pass over every triangle plus a binary search per particle — a few milliseconds for 9000 particles over 10k triangles — and it happens once per rebuild, never per frame.
- Two draw calls: the whole point cloud, and every measured ring in one `LineSegments` buffer. The rings do not depth-test, so their far halves cross in front of the shell; at hairline width and 0.3 opacity that reads as an orbit diagram rather than as an error.
- The rAF subscription is gated on `useInView` and `useVisibility`, so a scrolled-away or backgrounded instance stops paying for fill. The assembly resumes from wherever it froze rather than restarting.
- three constructs its own canvas, which is appended and removed per effect run. Reusing a React-owned `<canvas ref>` is unsafe here: cleanup calls `forceContextLoss()`, and under React 19 StrictMode the remount would hand the effect back the dead context, leaving the component permanently black.

## Definition of done

On entering view the shell builds from the base upward over about two seconds and holds, then turns slowly. Density is even everywhere: the small finial and the large knot carry the same particles-per-square-millimetre, with no dense speckle on the small parts. Particles nearer the camera are visibly larger than those on the far side, and none of them pop out of existence as the cloud turns. The rings hug the silhouette — they widen where the form widens — and do not cut through the middle of it. Resize the container from wide to narrow: the shell stays fully in frame and particles keep the same apparent size rather than growing or shrinking. With reduced motion a fully assembled three-quarter view renders immediately and holds still.

When you are finished, tell me which of the requirements above you implemented
and where, so I can check them.
